  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-129</h4>
  <h1 id="server-modified-values-and-defaults">Server-Modified Values and Defaults</h1>
<p>Services often provide default values for resource fields, and occasionally
normalize the user input before returning it in the response. The guidance
herein describes how services document such behavior for the benefit of
consumers.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<h3 id="single-owner-fields">Single Owner Fields</h3>
<p>Fields <strong>must</strong> have a single owner, whether that is the client or the server.
Server owned fields <strong>must</strong> be indicated with the <code>OUTPUT_ONLY</code> field_behavior.
All other types of fields <strong>must</strong> be considered to be owned by the client. The
server <strong>must</strong> respect the value (or lack thereof) for all client owned fields
and not modify them.</p>
<h3 id="effective-values">Effective Values</h3>
<p>There are instances where a service will allocate, generate, or calculate a
value if the client chooses not to specify one. For example: a client creates a
virtual machine without specifying a static IP address for the virtual machine
to be available on. Such a scenario is opting into dynamic IP address
allocation.</p>
<p>Some examples of these types of fields are ones that are:</p>
<ul>
<li>generated (UUID)</li>
<li>allocated (dynamic IP address)</li>
<li>assigned (most recent software package version)</li>
</ul>
<p>An attribute with an effective value <strong><em>must</em></strong> be expressed as two fields in
the API:</p>
<ul>
<li>a mutable field that can be optionally set by the user and <strong>must not</strong> be
modified by the service</li>
<li>an <code>OUTPUT_ONLY</code> field that records the effective value decided on by the
service</li>
</ul>
<p>Example:
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">VirtualMachine</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="err">…</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">ip_address</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">effective_ip_address</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OUTPUT_ONLY</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div></p>
<h4 id="naming">Naming</h4>
<p>Effective values <strong>must</strong> be named by prefixing <code>effective_</code> to the mutable
field's name.</p>
<h3 id="user-specified-fields">User-Specified Fields</h3>
<p>For user-specified fields, the value in response from the service <strong>must</strong> be
the same as provided by the create or update request. For string fields this
means returning the value unchanged, with one exception:</p>
<ul>
<li>When a string field has a data type annotation, a normalized string that
  represents the given value <strong>may</strong> be returned.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="normalizations">Normalizations</h3>
<p>A field that is normalized by the service <strong>must</strong> be annotated with the
<code>google.api.field_info</code> extension. See (<a href="/202">AIP-202</a>) for guidance on using
this extension The allowed set of normalizations includes the following formats:</p>
<ul>
<li>uuid</li>
<li>ipv4</li>
<li>ipv6</li>
<li>email</li>
</ul>
<p>Normalizations on fields <strong>must</strong> be described using the <code>google.api.field_info</code>
annotation.</p>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<p>Server-modified and default values often make it harder to implement
<a href="/9#declarative-clients">declarative clients</a>. These clients are often unable to
tell when their desired state matches the current state for these fields, as the
rules by which a server may modify and return values are complex, not public,
and not repeatable.</p>
<h3 id="rationale-for-single-owner-fields">Rationale for Single Owner Fields</h3>
<p>When fields do not have a single owner they can cause issues for
<a href="/9#declarative-clients">declarative clients</a>. These clients may attempt to set
values for fields that are overwritten by server set values, leading to the
client entering an infinite loop to correct the change.</p>
<h3 id="rationale-for-naming">Rationale for Naming</h3>
<p>Consistent naming is important for identifying standard behavior across APIs
and fields. Programmatic association between user-specified and effective values
depends on consistent naming.</p>
<h3 id="rationale-for-normalizations">Rationale for Normalizations</h3>
<p>Normalizations are important to allow services to store and return values in a
standard way while communicating to clients what changes are semantically
identical. Normalizing a value on the service side allows the service to accept
a wider range of semantically identical inputs without needing to maintain every
value as a raw string. Surfacing the normalization that is being applied to
clients allows for client side comparison of sent and retrieved values to check
for differences.</p>
<p>For example, in a resource that accepts an email address on a particular field
a client may specify a given email address in a variety of ways. For the email
<code>ada@example.com</code> a client may choose to specify <code>ADA@example.com</code>,
<code>aDa@example.com</code>, or <code>AdA@example.com</code>. These are semantically identical and
<em>should</em> all be accepted by the service. The service then may choose to
normalize the email address for storage and retrieval through downcasing or
canonicalization. Importantly, the information surfaced to clients on the
normalization of a field will not describe the normalization algorithm itself,
but instead the comparison method used to accurately compute if two values
should be considered equal.</p>
<h3 id="rationale-for-field-value-handling">Rationale for Field Value Handling</h3>
<p>For fields not using an allowed normalization,
<a href="/9#declarative-clients">Declarative clients</a> will not be able to identify which changes are
semantically meaningful. When a <a href="/9#declarative-clients">Declarative client</a>
sends a particular value it will ensure that the value is being returned by the
service to validate it was set correctly.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2023-10-31:</strong> Update to approved.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-130</h4>
  <h1 id="methods">Methods</h1>
<p>An API is composed of one or more methods, which represent a specific operation
that a service can perform on behalf of the consumer.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<h3 id="categories-of-methods">Categories of Methods</h3>
<p>The following enumerates multiple categories of methods that exist, often
grouped up under some object (e.g. collection or resource) that the method
operates upon.</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Category Name</th>
<th>Related AIPs</th>
<th><a href="/9#declarative-clients">Declarative client</a> integration</th>
<th>CLI / UI integration</th>
<th>SDK integration</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><em>Standard Methods</em></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Standard collection methods</strong>: operate on a collection of resources (List or Create).</td>
<td><a href="/121">AIP-121</a>, <a href="/132">AIP-132</a>, <a href="/133">AIP-133</a></td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Standard resource methods</strong>: fetch or mutate a single resource (Get, Update, Delete).</td>
<td><a href="/121">AIP-121</a>, <a href="/131">AIP-131</a>, <a href="/134">AIP-134</a>, <a href="/135">AIP-135</a></td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Batch resource methods</strong>: fetch or mutate multiple resources in a collection by name.</td>
<td><a href="/231">AIP-231</a>, <a href="/233">AIP-233</a>, <a href="/234">AIP-234</a>, <a href="/235">AIP-235</a></td>
<td>may be used to optimize queries</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Aggregated list methods</strong>: fetch or mutate multiple resources of the same type across multiple collections.</td>
<td><a href="/159">AIP-159</a></td>
<td>not useful nor automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><em>Custom Fetch Methods</em></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Custom collection fetch methods</strong>: fetch information across a collection that cannot be expressed via a standard method.</td>
<td><a href="/136">AIP-136</a></td>
<td>handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Custom resource fetch methods</strong>: fetch information for a single resource that cannot be expressed via a standard method.</td>
<td><a href="/136">AIP-136</a></td>
<td>handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><em>Custom Mutation Methods</em></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Backing up a resource</strong>: storing a copy of a resource at a particular point in time.</td>
<td><a href="/162">AIP-162</a></td>
<td>unused or handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Restoring a resource</strong>: setting a resource to a version from a particular point in time.</td>
<td><a href="/162">AIP-162</a></td>
<td>unused or handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Renaming a resource</strong>: modify the resource's name or id while preserving configuration and data.</td>
<td><a href="/136">AIP-136</a></td>
<td>unused or handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Custom collection mutation methods</strong>: perform an imperative operation referencing a collection that may mutate one or more resources within that collection in fashion that cannot be easily achieved by standard methods (e.g. state transitions).</td>
<td><a href="/136">AIP-136</a></td>
<td>unused or handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Custom resource mutation methods</strong>: perform an imperative operation on a resource that may mutate it in a way a standard method cannot (e.g. state transitions).</td>
<td><a href="/136">AIP-136</a></td>
<td>unused or handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><em>Misc Custom Methods</em></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Stateless Methods</strong>: a method that has no permanent effect on any data within the API (e.g. translating text)</td>
<td><a href="/136">AIP-136</a></td>
<td>unused or handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><em>None of the above</em></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Streaming methods</strong>: methods that communicate via client, server, or bi-directional streams.</td>
<td></td>
<td>handwritten</td>
<td>handwritten</td>
<td>automatable</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h3 id="choosing-a-method-category">Choosing a method category</h3>
<p>While designing a method, API authors should choose from the defined categories
in the following order:</p>
<ol>
<li>Standard methods (on collections and resources)</li>
<li>Standard batch or aggregate methods</li>
<li>Custom methods (on collections, resources, or stateless)</li>
<li>Streaming methods</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<p>Resource-oriented standard and custom methods are recommended first, as they can
be expressed in the widest variety of clients (Declarative clients, CLIs, UIs, and so on), and
offer the most uniform experience that allows users to apply their knowledge of
one API to another.</p>
<p>If a standard method is unsuitable, then custom methods (that are mounted to a
resource or collection) offer a lesser, but still valuable level of consistency,
helping the user reason about the scope of the action and the object whose
configuration is read to inform that action. Although mutative custom methods
are not uniform enough to have a automated integration with exclusively
resource-oriented clients such as <a href="/9#declarative-clients">Declarative client</a>s, they are still a pattern that
can easily recognized by CLIs, UIs, and SDKs.</p>
<p>If one cannot express their APIs in a resource-oriented fashion at all, then the
operation falls in a category where the lack of uniformity makes it difficult
for any client aside from SDKs to model the operation. This category is
preferred last due to the fact that a user cannot rely on their knowledge of
similar APIs, as well as the issue that integration with many clients will
likely have to be hand-written.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2023-09-05</strong>: Update to approved.</li>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-131</h4>
  <h1 id="standard-methods-get">Standard methods: Get</h1>
<p>In REST APIs, it is customary to make a <code>GET</code> request to a resource's URI (for
example, <code>/v1/publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</code>) in order to retrieve that
resource.</p>
<p>Resource-oriented design (<a href="/121">AIP-121</a>) honors this pattern through the <code>Get</code>
method. These RPCs accept the URI representing that resource and return the
resource.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>must</strong> provide a get method for resources. The purpose of the get method
is to return data from a single resource.</p>
<p>Get methods are specified using the following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">GetBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">GetBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">get</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{name=publishers/*/books/*}&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.method_signature</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;name&quot;</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with the word <code>Get</code>. The remainder of the RPC
  name <strong>should</strong> be the singular form of the resource's message name.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with a <code>Request</code> suffix.</li>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> be the resource itself. (There is no
  <code>GetBookResponse</code>.)<ul>
<li>The response <strong>should</strong> usually include the fully-populated resource unless
  there is a reason to return a partial response (see <a href="/157">AIP-157</a>).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>GET</code>.</li>
<li>The URI <strong>should</strong> contain a single variable field corresponding to the
  resource name.<ul>
<li>This field <strong>should</strong> be called <code>name</code>.</li>
<li>The URI <strong>should</strong> have a variable corresponding to this field.</li>
<li>The <code>name</code> field <strong>should</strong> be the only variable in the URI path. All
  remaining parameters <strong>should</strong> map to URI query parameters.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>There <strong>must not</strong> be a <code>body</code> key in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation.</li>
<li>There <strong>should</strong> be exactly one <code>google.api.method_signature</code> annotation,
  with a value of <code>"name"</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>Get methods implement a common request message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">GetBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The name of the book to retrieve.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A resource name field <strong>must</strong> be included. It <strong>should</strong> be called <code>name</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The comment for the <code>name</code> field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in
  another AIP.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> The <code>name</code> field in the request object corresponds to the <code>name</code>
variable in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation on the RPC. This causes the <code>name</code>
field in the request to be populated based on the value in the URL when the
REST/JSON interface is used.</p>
<h3 id="errors">Errors</h3>
<p>See <a href="/193">errors</a>, in particular <a href="/193#permission-denied">when to use PERMISSION_DENIED and
NOT_FOUND errors</a>.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2023-03-17</strong>: Align with <a href="/122">AIP-122</a> and make Get a must.</li>
<li><strong>2022-11-04</strong>: Aggregated error guidance to <a href="/193">AIP-193</a>.</li>
<li><strong>2022-06-02</strong>: Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2020-06-08</strong>: Added guidance on returning the full resource.</li>
<li><strong>2019-10-18</strong>: Added guidance on annotations.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-12</strong>: Added guidance for error cases.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
<li><strong>2019-05-29</strong>: Added an explicit prohibition on arbitrary fields in standard
  methods.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-132</h4>
  <h1 id="standard-methods-list">Standard methods: List</h1>
<p>In many APIs, it is customary to make a <code>GET</code> request to a collection's URI
(for example, <code>/v1/publishers/1/books</code>) in order to retrieve a list of
resources, each of which lives within that collection.</p>
<p>Resource-oriented design (<a href="/121">AIP-121</a>) honors this pattern through the <code>List</code>
method. These RPCs accept the parent collection (and potentially some other
parameters), and return a list of responses matching that input.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>must</strong> provide a <code>List</code> method for resources unless the resource is a
<a href="/156">singleton</a>. The purpose of the <code>List</code> method is to return data from a finite
collection (generally singular unless the operation supports <a href="/159">reading across
collections</a>).</p>
<p>List methods are specified using the following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ListBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ListBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ListBooksResponse</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">get</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.method_signature</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;parent&quot;</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with the word <code>List</code>. The remainder of the RPC
  name <strong>should</strong> be the plural form of the resource being listed.</li>
<li>The request and response messages <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with
  <code>Request</code> and <code>Response</code> suffixes.</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>GET</code>.</li>
<li>The collection whose resources are being listed <strong>should</strong> map to the URI
  path.<ul>
<li>The collection's parent resource <strong>should</strong> be called <code>parent</code>, and
  <strong>should</strong> be the only variable in the URI path. All remaining parameters
  <strong>should</strong> map to URI query parameters.</li>
<li>The collection identifier (<code>books</code> in the above example) <strong>must</strong> be a
  literal string.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The <code>body</code> key in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation <strong>must</strong> be omitted.</li>
<li>If the resource being listed is not a top-level resource, there <strong>should</strong>
  be exactly one <code>google.api.method_signature</code> annotation, with a value of
  <code>"parent"</code>. If the resource being listed is a top-level resource, there
  <strong>should</strong> be either no <code>google.api.method_signature</code> annotation, or exactly
  one <code>google.api.method_signature</code> annotation, with a value of <code>""</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>List methods implement a common request message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ListBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent, which owns this collection of books.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The maximum number of books to return. The service may return fewer than</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// this value.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If unspecified, at most 50 books will be returned.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The maximum value is 1000; values above 1000 will be coerced to 1000.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">int32</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">page_size</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A page token, received from a previous `ListBooks` call.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// When paginating, all other parameters provided to `ListBooks` must match</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// the call that provided the page token.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">page_token</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>must</strong> be included unless the resource being listed is a
  top-level resource. It <strong>should</strong> be called <code>parent</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> of the resource
  being listed.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The <code>page_size</code> and <code>page_token</code> fields, which support pagination, <strong>must</strong>
  be specified on all list request messages. For more information, see
  <a href="/158">AIP-158</a>.<ul>
<li>The comment above the <code>page_size</code> field <strong>should</strong> document the maximum
  allowed value, as well as the default value if the field is omitted (or set
  to <code>0</code>). If preferred, the API <strong>may</strong> state that the server will use a
  sensible default. This default <strong>may</strong> change over time.</li>
<li>If a user provides a value greater than the maximum allowed value, the API
  <strong>should</strong> coerce the value to the maximum allowed.</li>
<li>If a user provides a negative or other invalid value, the API <strong>must</strong> send
  an <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code> error.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The <code>page_token</code> field <strong>must</strong> be included on all list request messages.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>may</strong> include fields for common design patterns
  relevant to list methods, such as <code>string filter</code> and <code>string order_by</code>.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> List methods <strong>should</strong> return the same results for any user that has
permission to make a successful List request on the collection. Search methods
are more relaxed on this.</p>
<h3 id="response-message">Response message</h3>
<p>List methods implement a common response message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ListBooksResponse</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The books from the specified publisher.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">books</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A token, which can be sent as `page_token` to retrieve the next page.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this field is omitted, there are no subsequent pages.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">next_page_token</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> include one repeated field corresponding to the
  resources being returned, and <strong>should not</strong> include any other repeated
  fields unless described in another AIP (for example, <a href="/217">AIP-217</a>).<ul>
<li>The response <strong>should</strong> usually include fully-populated resources unless
  there is a reason to return a partial response (see <a href="/157">AIP-157</a>).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The <code>next_page_token</code> field, which supports pagination, <strong>must</strong> be included
  on all list response messages. It <strong>must</strong> be set if there are subsequent
  pages, and <strong>must not</strong> be set if the response represents the final page. For
  more information, see <a href="/158">AIP-158</a>.</li>
<li>The message <strong>may</strong> include a <code>int32 total_size</code> (or <code>int64 total_size</code>)
  field with the number of items in the collection.<ul>
<li>The value <strong>may</strong> be an estimate (the field <strong>should</strong> clearly document
  this if so).</li>
<li>If filtering is used, the <code>total_size</code> field <strong>should</strong> reflect the size of
  the collection <em>after</em> the filter is applied.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="ordering">Ordering</h3>
<p><code>List</code> methods <strong>may</strong> allow clients to specify sorting order; if they do, the
request message <strong>should</strong> contain a <code>string order_by</code> field.</p>
<ul>
<li>Values <strong>should</strong> be a comma separated list of fields. For example:
  <code>"foo,bar"</code>.</li>
<li>The default sorting order is ascending. To specify descending order for a
  field, users append a <code>" desc"</code> suffix; for example: <code>"foo desc, bar"</code>.</li>
<li>Redundant space characters in the syntax are insignificant.
  <code>"foo, bar desc"</code>, <code>" foo , bar desc "</code>, and <code>"foo,bar desc"</code> are all
  equivalent.</li>
<li>Subfields are specified with a <code>.</code> character, such as <code>foo.bar</code> or
  <code>address.street</code>.</li>
<li>The resulting list order <strong>should</strong> be based on the field type's natural
  comparator e.g. numerics ordered numerically, strings ordered
  lexicographically, etc. However, APIs <strong>may</strong> choose to use a different
  ordering; if so, it <strong>must</strong> be documented in the <code>order_by</code> definition.<ul>
<li>Furthermore, <a href="https://protobuf.dev/reference/protobuf/google.protobuf">well-known</a> types, like <code>Timestamp</code> and <code>Duration</code> are
  compared as their representative type; <code>Timestamp</code> is compared as time e.g.
  before or after, <code>Duration</code> is compared as a quantity e.g. more or less.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<!-- TODO(#220): Add a reference to [AIP-161](/161) once it is written. -->

<p><strong>Note:</strong> Only include ordering if there is an established need to do so. It is
always possible to add ordering later, but removing it is a breaking change.</p>
<h3 id="filtering">Filtering</h3>
<p>List methods <strong>may</strong> allow clients to specify filters; if they do, the request
message <strong>should</strong> contain a <code>string filter</code> field. Filtering is described in
more detail in <a href="/160">AIP-160</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Only include filtering if there is an established need to do so. It
is always possible to add filtering later, but removing it is a breaking
change.</p>
<h3 id="soft-deleted-resources">Soft-deleted resources</h3>
<p>Some APIs need to "<a href="/135#soft-delete">soft delete</a>" resources, marking them as deleted or
pending deletion (and optionally purging them later).</p>
<p>APIs that do this <strong>should not</strong> include deleted resources by default in list
requests. APIs with soft deletion of a resource <strong>should</strong> include a
<code>bool show_deleted</code> field in the list request that, if set, will cause
soft-deleted resources to be included.</p>
<h3 id="errors">Errors</h3>
<p>See <a href="/193">errors</a>, in particular <a href="/193#permission-denied">when to use PERMISSION_DENIED and
NOT_FOUND errors</a>.</p>
<h2 id="further-reading">Further reading</h2>
<ul>
<li>For details on pagination, see <a href="/158">AIP-158</a>.</li>
<li>For listing across multiple parent collections, see <a href="/159">AIP-159</a>.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li><strong>2025-02-25</strong>: Require documentation for ordering not matching field type
  with clarification on ordering of well-known types.</li>
<li><strong>2023-03-22</strong>: Fix guidance wording to mention <a href="/159">AIP-159</a>.</li>
<li><strong>2023-03-17</strong>: Align with <a href="/122">AIP-122</a> and make Get a must.</li>
<li><strong>2022-11-04</strong>: Aggregated error guidance to <a href="/193">AIP-193</a>.</li>
<li><strong>2022-06-02</strong>: Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2020-09-02</strong>: Add link to the filtering AIP.</li>
<li><strong>2020-08-14</strong>: Added error guidance for permission denied cases.</li>
<li><strong>2020-06-08</strong>: Added guidance on returning the full resource.</li>
<li><strong>2020-05-19</strong>: Removed requirement to document ordering behavior.</li>
<li><strong>2020-04-15</strong>: Added guidance on List permissions.</li>
<li><strong>2019-10-18</strong>: Added guidance on annotations.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
<li><strong>2019-07-30</strong>: Added guidance about documenting the ordering behavior.</li>
<li><strong>2019-05-29</strong>: Added an explicit prohibition on arbitrary fields in standard
  methods.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-133</h4>
  <h1 id="standard-methods-create">Standard methods: Create</h1>
<p>In REST APIs, it is customary to make a <code>POST</code> request to a collection's URI
(for example, <code>/v1/publishers/{publisher}/books</code>) in order to create a new
resource within that collection.</p>
<p>Resource-oriented design (<a href="/121">AIP-121</a>) honors this pattern through the <code>Create</code>
method. These RPCs accept the parent collection and the resource to create (and
potentially some other parameters), and return the created resource.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>should</strong> generally provide a create method for resources unless it is
not valuable for users to do so. The purpose of the create method is to create
a new resource in an already-existing collection.</p>
<p>Create methods are specified using the following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">CreateBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">CreateBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.method_signature</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;parent,book&quot;</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with the word <code>Create</code>. The remainder of the
  RPC name <strong>should</strong> be the singular form of the resource being created.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with a <code>Request</code> suffix.</li>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> be the resource itself. There is no
  <code>CreateBookResponse</code>.<ul>
<li>The response <strong>should</strong> include the fully-populated resource, and <strong>must</strong>
  include any fields that were provided unless they are input only (see
  <a href="/203">AIP-203</a>) or there is a reason to return a partial response (see
  <a href="/157">AIP-157</a>).</li>
<li>If the create RPC is <a href="#long-running-create">long-running</a>, the response
  message <strong>must</strong> be a <code>google.longrunning.Operation</code> which resolves to the
  resource itself.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>POST</code>.</li>
<li>The collection where the resource is being added <strong>should</strong> map to the URI
  path.<ul>
<li>The collection's parent resource <strong>should</strong> be called <code>parent</code>, and
  <strong>should</strong> be the only variable in the URI path.</li>
<li>The collection identifier (<code>books</code> in the above example) <strong>must</strong> be
  a literal string.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>There <strong>must</strong> be a <code>body</code> key in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation, and it
  <strong>must</strong> map to the resource field in the request message.<ul>
<li>All remaining fields <strong>should</strong> map to URI query parameters.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>There <strong>should</strong> be exactly one <code>google.api.method_signature</code> annotation,
  with a value of <code>"parent,{resource},{resource}_id"</code>, or "<code>"parent,{resource}"</code>
  if the resource ID is not required.</li>
<li>If the API is operating on the <a href="/111#management-plane">management plane</a>, the operation should have
  <a href="/121#strong-consistency">strong consistency</a>: the completion of a create operation <strong>must</strong> mean
  that all user-settable values and the existence of the resource have reached a
  steady-state and reading resource state returns a consistent response.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>Create methods implement a common request message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">CreateBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent resource where this book will be created.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The ID to use for the book, which will become the final component of</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// the book&#39;s resource name.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// This value should be 4-63 characters, and valid characters</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// are /[a-z][0-9]-/.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">book_id</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The book to create.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>must</strong> be included unless the resource being created is a
  top-level resource. It <strong>should</strong> be called <code>parent</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> of the resource
  being created.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>A <code>{resource}_id</code> field <strong>must</strong> be included for management plane resources,
  and <strong>should</strong> be included for data plane resources.</li>
<li>The resource field <strong>must</strong> be included and <strong>must</strong> map to the POST body.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="long-running-create">Long-running create</h3>
<p>Some resources take longer to create a resource than is reasonable for a
regular API request. In this situation, the API <strong>should</strong> use a long-running
operation (<a href="/151">AIP-151</a>) instead:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">CreateBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">CreateBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;OperationMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The response type <strong>must</strong> be set to the resource (what the return type would
  be if the RPC was not long-running).</li>
<li>Both the <code>response_type</code> and <code>metadata_type</code> fields <strong>must</strong> be specified.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Important:</strong> Declarative-friendly resources (<a href="/128">AIP-128</a>) <strong>should</strong> use
long-running operations. The service <strong>may</strong> return an LRO that is already set
to done if the request is effectively immediate.</p>
<h3 id="user-specified-ids">User-specified IDs</h3>
<p>An API <strong>must</strong> allow a user to specify the ID component of a resource (the last
segment of the resource name) on creation if the API is operating on the
<a href="/111#management-plane">management plane</a>.</p>
<p>On the <a href="/111#data-plane">data plane</a>, an API <strong>should</strong> allow a user to specify the ID.
Exceptional cases should have the following behavior:</p>
<ul>
<li>The data plane resource allows identical records without a need to
  disambiguate between the two (e.g. rows in a table with no primary key).</li>
<li>The data plane resource will not be exposed in <a href="/9#declarative-clients">Declarative clients</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>An API
<strong>may</strong> allow the <code>{resource}_id</code> field have the <a href="/203">field_behavior</a> <code>OPTIONAL</code>,
and generate a system-generated ID if one is not specified.</p>
<p>For example:</p>
<div class="highlight language-None"><pre><span></span><code>// Using user-specified IDs.
publishers/lacroix/books/les-miserables

// Using system-generated IDs.
publishers/012345678-abcd-cdef/books/12341234-5678-abcd
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The <code>{resource}_id</code> field <strong>must</strong> exist on the request message, not the
  resource itself.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>may</strong> be required or optional. If it is required, it <strong>should</strong>
  include the corresponding annotation.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The <code>name</code> field on the resource <strong>must</strong> be ignored.</li>
<li>There <strong>should</strong> be exactly one <code>google.api.method_signature</code> annotation on
  the RPC, with a value of <code>"parent,{resource},{resource}_id"</code> if the resource
  being created is not a top-level resource, or with a value of
  <code>"{resource},{resource}_id"</code> if the resource being created is a top-level
  resource.</li>
<li>The documentation <strong>should</strong> explain what the acceptable format is, and the
  format <strong>should</strong> follow the guidance for resource name formatting in
  <a href="/122">AIP-122</a>.</li>
<li>If a user tries to create a resource with an ID that would result in a
  duplicate resource name, the service <strong>must</strong> error with <code>ALREADY_EXISTS</code>.<ul>
<li>However, if the user making the call does not have permission to see the
  duplicate resource, the service <strong>must</strong> error with <code>PERMISSION_DENIED</code>
  instead.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> For REST APIs, the user-specified ID field, <code>{resource}_id</code>,
is provided as a query parameters on the request URI.</p>
<h3 id="errors">Errors</h3>
<p>See <a href="/193">errors</a>, in particular <a href="/193#permission-denied">when to use PERMISSION_DENIED and
NOT_FOUND errors</a>.</p>
<h2 id="further-reading">Further reading</h2>
<ul>
<li>For ensuring idempotency in <code>Create</code> methods, see <a href="/155">AIP-155</a>.</li>
<li>For naming resources involving Unicode, see <a href="/210">AIP-210</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="requiring-user-specified-ids">Requiring user-specified ids</h3>
<p><a href="/9#declarative-clients">Declarative clients</a> use the resource ID as a way to identify a resource for
applying updates and for conflict resolution. The lack of a user-specified ID
means a client is unable to find the resource unless they store the identifier
locally, and can result in re-creating the resource. This in turn has a
downstream effect on all resources that reference it, forcing them to update to
the ID of the newly-created resource.</p>
<p>Having a user-specified ID also means the client can precalculate the resource
name and use it in references from other resources.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2025-10-03</strong>: Allow use of partial responses via <a href="/157">AIP-157</a>.</li>
<li><strong>2023-10-20</strong>: Clarify that {resource}_id is only required for management plane resources.</li>
<li><strong>2023-08-24</strong>: Adding consistency requirement.</li>
<li><strong>2023-05-11</strong>: Changing guidance around resource_id to a must.</li>
<li><strong>2022-11-04</strong>: Referencing aggregated error guidance in <a href="/193">AIP-193</a>, similar to
  other CRUDL AIPs.</li>
<li><strong>2022-06-02</strong>: Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2020-10-06</strong>: Added declarative-friendly guidance.</li>
<li><strong>2020-08-14</strong>: Updated error guidance to use permission denied over
  forbidden.</li>
<li><strong>2020-06-08</strong>: Added guidance on returning the full resource.</li>
<li><strong>2019-11-22</strong>: Added clarification on what error to use if a duplicate name
  is sent.</li>
<li><strong>2019-10-18</strong>: Added guidance on annotations.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
<li><strong>2019-06-10</strong>: Added guidance for long-running create.</li>
<li><strong>2019-05-29</strong>: Added an explicit prohibition on arbitrary fields in standard
  methods.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-134</h4>
  <h1 id="standard-methods-update">Standard methods: Update</h1>
<p>In REST APIs, it is customary to make a <code>PATCH</code> or <code>PUT</code> request to a
resource's URI (for example, <code>/v1/publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</code>) in
order to update that resource.</p>
<p>Resource-oriented design (<a href="/121">AIP-121</a>) honors this pattern through the <code>Update</code>
method (which mirrors the REST <code>PATCH</code> behavior). These RPCs accept the URI
representing that resource and return the resource.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>should</strong> generally provide an update method for resources unless it is
not valuable for users to do so. The purpose of the update method is to make
changes to the resources without causing side effects.</p>
<p>Update methods are specified using the following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">UpdateBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">UpdateBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">patch</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{book.name=publishers/*/books/*}&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.method_signature</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;book,update_mask&quot;</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with the word <code>Update</code>. The remainder of the
  RPC name <strong>should</strong> be the singular form of the resource's message name.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with a <code>Request</code> suffix.</li>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> be the resource itself. (There is no
  <code>UpdateBookResponse</code>.)<ul>
<li>The response <strong>should</strong> include the fully-populated resource, and <strong>must</strong>
  include any fields that were sent and included in the update mask unless
  they are input only (see <a href="/203">AIP-203</a>) or there is a reason to return a partial
  response (see <a href="/157">AIP-157</a>).</li>
<li>If the update RPC is <a href="#long-running-update">long-running</a>, the response
  message <strong>must</strong> be a <code>google.longrunning.Operation</code> which resolves to the
  resource itself.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The method <strong>should</strong> support partial resource update, and the HTTP verb
  <strong>should</strong> be <code>PATCH</code>.<ul>
<li>If the method will only ever support full resource replacement, then the
  HTTP verb <strong>may</strong> be <code>PUT</code>. However, this is strongly discouraged because
  it becomes a backwards-incompatible change to add fields to the resource.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The resource's <code>name</code> field <strong>should</strong> map to the URI path.<ul>
<li>The <code>{resource}.name</code> field <strong>should</strong> be the only variable in the URI
  path.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>There <strong>must</strong> be a <code>body</code> key in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation, and it
  <strong>must</strong> map to the resource field in the request message.<ul>
<li>All remaining fields <strong>should</strong> map to URI query parameters.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>There <strong>should</strong> be exactly one <code>google.api.method_signature</code> annotation, with
  a value of <code>"{resource},update_mask"</code>.</li>
<li>If the API is operating on the <a href="/111#management-plane">management plane</a>, the operation should have
  <a href="/121#strong-consistency">strong consistency</a>: the completion of an update operation <strong>must</strong> mean
  that all user-settable values and the existence of the resource have reached a
  steady-state and reading resource state returns a consistent response.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Unlike the other four standard methods, the URI path here references
a nested field (<code>book.name</code>) in the example. If the resource field has a word
separator, <code>snake_case</code> is used.</p>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>Update methods implement a common request message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">UpdateBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The book to update.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The book&#39;s `name` field is used to identify the book to update.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The list of fields to update.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">google.protobuf.FieldMask</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">update_mask</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> contain a field for the resource.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> map to the <code>PATCH</code> body.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>A <code>name</code> field <strong>must</strong> be included in the resource message. It <strong>should</strong>
  be called <code>name</code>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> of the resource
  being updated.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If partial resource update is supported, a field mask <strong>must</strong> be included.
  It <strong>must</strong> be of type <code>google.protobuf.FieldMask</code>, and it <strong>must</strong> be
  called <code>update_mask</code>.<ul>
<li>The fields used in the field mask correspond to the resource being updated
  (not the request message).</li>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> be optional, and the service <strong>must</strong> treat an omitted
  field mask as an implied field mask equivalent to all fields that are
  populated (have a non-empty value).</li>
<li>Update masks <strong>must</strong> support a special value <code>*</code>, meaning full replacement
  (the equivalent of <code>PUT</code>).<ul>
<li>API producers need to be conscious of how adding new, mutable fields to a
  resource will be handled when consumers use <code>*</code> without knowledge of said
  new, mutable fields. Likewise consumers need to use <code>*</code> only when the
  risks of doing so are acceptable. In general, it is safest to explicitly
  specify the fields to update rather than use <code>*</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="side-effects">Side effects</h3>
<p>In general, update methods are intended to update the data within the resource.
Update methods <strong>should not</strong> trigger other side effects. Instead, side effects
<strong>should</strong> be triggered by custom methods.</p>
<p>In particular, this entails that <a href="/216">state fields</a> <strong>must not</strong> be directly
writable in update methods.</p>
<h3 id="patch-and-put">PATCH and PUT</h3>
<p><strong>TL;DR:</strong> Google APIs generally use the <code>PATCH</code> HTTP verb only, and do not
support <code>PUT</code> requests.</p>
<p>We standardize on <code>PATCH</code> because Google updates stable APIs in place with
backwards-compatible improvements. It is often necessary to add a new field to
an existing resource, but this becomes a breaking change when using <code>PUT</code>.</p>
<p>To illustrate this, consider a <code>PUT</code> request to a <code>Book</code> resource:</p>
<pre><code>  PUT /v1/publishers/123/books/456

  {"title": "Mary Poppins", "author": "P.L. Travers"}
</code></pre>
<p>Next consider that the resource is later augmented with a new field (here we
add <code>rating</code>):</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">title</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">author</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Subsequently added to v1 in place...</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">int32</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">rating</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>If a rating is set on a book and the existing <code>PUT</code> request was executed, it
would wipe out the book's rating. In essence, a <code>PUT</code> request unintentionally
wiped out data because the previous version did not know about it.</p>
<h3 id="long-running-update">Long-running update</h3>
<p>Some resources take longer to update a resource than is reasonable for a
regular API request. In this situation, the API <strong>should</strong> use a long-running
operation (<a href="/151">AIP-151</a>) instead:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">UpdateBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">UpdateBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">patch</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{book.name=publishers/*/books/*}&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;OperationMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The response type <strong>must</strong> be set to the resource (what the return type would
  be if the RPC was not long-running).</li>
<li>Both the <code>response_type</code> and <code>metadata_type</code> fields <strong>must</strong> be specified.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Declarative-friendly resources (<a href="/128">AIP-128</a>) <strong>should</strong> use long-running
update.</p>
<h3 id="create-or-update">Create or update</h3>
<p>If the service uses client-assigned resource names, <code>Update</code> methods <strong>may</strong>
expose a <code>bool allow_missing</code> field, which will cause the method to succeed in
the event that the user attempts to update a resource that is not present (and
will create the resource in the process):</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">UpdateBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The book to update.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The book&#39;s `name` field is used to identify the book to be updated.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The list of fields to be updated.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">google.protobuf.FieldMask</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">update_mask</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If set to true, and the book is not found, a new book will be created.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// In this situation, `update_mask` is ignored.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">bool</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">allow_missing</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>More specifically, the <code>allow_missing</code> flag triggers the following behavior:</p>
<ul>
<li>If the method call is on a resource that does not exist, the resource is
  created. All fields are applied regardless of any provided field mask.<ul>
<li>However, if any required fields are missing or fields have invalid values,
  an <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code> error is returned.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If the method call is on a resource that already exists, and all fields
  match, the existing resource is returned unchanged.</li>
<li>If the method call is on a resource that already exists, only fields declared
  in the field mask are updated.</li>
</ul>
<p>The user <strong>must</strong> have the update permissions to call <code>Update</code> even with
<code>allow_missing</code> set to <code>true</code>. For customers that want to prevent users from
creating resources using the update method, IAM conditions <strong>should</strong> be used.</p>
<h3 id="etags">Etags</h3>
<p>An API may sometimes need to allow users to send update requests which are
guaranteed to be made against the most current data (a common use case for this
is to detect and avoid race conditions). Resources which need to enable this do
so by including a <code>string etag</code> field, which contains an opaque,
server-computed value representing the content of the resource.</p>
<p>In this situation, the resource <strong>should</strong> contain a <code>string etag</code> field:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pattern</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The resource name of the book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">IDENTIFIER</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The title of the book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Example: &quot;Mary Poppins&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">title</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The author of the book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Example: &quot;P.L. Travers&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">author</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The etag for this book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this is provided on update, it must match the server&#39;s etag.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">etag</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>The <code>etag</code> field <strong>may</strong> be either <a href="/203#required">required</a> or <a href="/203#optional">optional</a>. If it is set,
then the request <strong>must</strong> succeed if and only if the provided etag matches the
server-computed value, and <strong>must</strong> fail with an <code>ABORTED</code> error otherwise. The
<code>update_mask</code> field in the request does not affect the behavior of the <code>etag</code>
field, as it is not a field <em>being</em> updated.</p>
<h3 id="expensive-fields">Expensive fields</h3>
<p>APIs sometimes encounter situations where some fields on a resource are
expensive or impossible to reliably return.</p>
<p>This can happen in a few situations:</p>
<ul>
<li>A resource may have some fields that are very expensive to compute, and that
  are generally not useful to the customer on update requests.</li>
<li>A single resource sometimes represents an amalgamation of data from multiple
  underlying (and eventually consistent) data sources. In these situations, it
  is impossible to return authoritative information on the fields that were not
  changed.</li>
</ul>
<p>In this situation, an API <strong>may</strong> return back only the fields that were
updated, and omit the rest, and <strong>should</strong> document this behavior if they do
so.</p>
<h3 id="errors">Errors</h3>
<p>See <a href="/193">errors</a>, in particular <a href="/193#permission-denied">when to use PERMISSION_DENIED and
NOT_FOUND errors</a>.</p>
<p>In addition, if the user does have proper permission, but the requested resource
does not exist, the service <strong>must</strong> error with <code>NOT_FOUND</code> (HTTP 404) unless
<code>allow_missing</code> is set to <code>true</code>.</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>2025-10-03</strong>: Allow use of partial responses via <a href="/157">AIP-157</a>.</li>

<li><strong>2024-03-14</strong>: Make <code>update_mask</code> optional field_behaviour guidance a <strong>must</strong>.</li>
<li><strong>2023-08-26</strong>: Adding consistency requirement.</li>
<li><strong>2023-07-17</strong>: Make <code>update_mask</code> name guidance a <strong>must</strong>.</li>
<li><strong>2022-11-04</strong>: Aggregated error guidance to <a href="/193">AIP-193</a>.</li>
<li><strong>2022-06-02</strong>: Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2021-11-04</strong>: Changed the permission check if <code>allow_missing</code> is set.</li>
<li><strong>2021-07-08</strong>: Added error guidance for resource not found case.</li>
<li><strong>2021-03-05</strong>: Changed the etag error from <code>FAILED_PRECONDITION</code> (which
  becomes HTTP 400) to <code>ABORTED</code> (409).</li>
<li><strong>2020-10-06</strong>: Added guidance for declarative-friendly resources.</li>
<li><strong>2020-10-06</strong>: Added guidance for <code>allow_missing</code>.</li>
<li><strong>2020-08-14</strong>: Added error guidance for permission denied cases.</li>
<li><strong>2020-06-08</strong>: Added guidance on returning the full resource.</li>
<li><strong>2019-10-18</strong>: Added guidance on annotations.</li>
<li><strong>2019-09-10</strong>: Added a link to the long-running operations AIP
  (<a href="/151">AIP-151</a>).</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
<li><strong>2019-06-10</strong>: Added guidance for long-running update.</li>
<li><strong>2019-05-29</strong>: Added an explicit prohibition on arbitrary fields in standard
  methods.</li>
</ul>
