  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-153</h4>
  <h1 id="import-and-export">Import and export</h1>
<p>Many users want to be able to load data into an API, or get their existing data
out of an API. This is particularly important for enterprise users, who are
often concerned about vendor lock-in.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> support import and export operations, which <strong>may</strong> create
multiple new resources, or they <strong>may</strong> populate data into a single resource.</p>
<h3 id="multiple-resources">Multiple resources</h3>
<p>Services <strong>may</strong> support importing and exporting multiple resources into or out
of an API, and <strong>should</strong> implement a common pattern to do so:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ImportBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ImportBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:import&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;ImportBooksResponse&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;ImportBooksMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ExportBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ExportBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:export&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;ExportBooksResponse&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;ExportBooksMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The method <strong>must</strong> return a long-running operation (see <a href="/151">AIP-151</a>) unless
  the service can guarantee that it will <em>never</em> need more than a few seconds
  to complete.</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>POST</code>, and the <code>body</code> <strong>must</strong> be <code>"*"</code>.</li>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included as part of the URI.<ul>
<li>If importing into or exporting from multiple resources is required, the API
  <strong>should</strong> keep the <code>parent</code> field and allow the user to use the <code>-</code>
  character to indicate multiple parents (see <a href="/159">AIP-159</a>).</li>
<li>On import, if the user provides a specific parent, the API <strong>must</strong> reject
  any imported resources that would be added to a different parent.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The URI suffix <strong>should</strong> be <code>:import</code> or <code>:export</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="data-for-a-single-resource">Data for a single resource</h3>
<p>Services <strong>may</strong> support importing and exporting data into or out of a single
resource, and <strong>should</strong> implement a common pattern to do so:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ImportPages</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ImportPagesRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{book=publishers/*/books/*}:importPages&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;ImportPagesResponse&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;ImportPagesMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ExportPages</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ExportPagesRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{book=publishers/*/books/*}:exportPages&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;ExportPagesResponse&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;ExportPagesMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The method <strong>must</strong> return a long-running operation (see <a href="/151">AIP-151</a>) unless
  the service can guarantee that it will <em>never</em> need more than a few seconds
  to complete.</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>POST</code>, and the <code>body</code> <strong>must</strong> be <code>"*"</code>.</li>
<li>A field representing the resource that data is being imported into <strong>should</strong>
  be included as part of the URI. The field <strong>should</strong> be named after the
  resource (and <strong>should not</strong> be called <code>name</code>).</li>
<li>The URI suffix should include both the verb and a noun for the data itself,
  such as <code>:importPages</code> or <code>:exportPages</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-object">Request object</h3>
<p>Imports and exports often require two fundamentally different types of
configuration:</p>
<ol>
<li>Configuration specific to the source or destination.</li>
<li>Configuration regarding the imported or exported data itself.</li>
</ol>
<p>Source or destination configuration should be grouped into a single message and
placed inside a oneof:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ImportBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">oneof</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">source</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">AuthorSource</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">author_source</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">TranslatorSource</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">translator_source</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">isbn_prefix</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ExportBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">oneof</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">destination</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">PrinterDestination</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">printer_destination</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">TranslatorDestination</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">translator_destination</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">filter</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The source configuration messages <strong>must</strong> be placed within a <code>oneof source</code>
  (for import) or <code>oneof destination</code> (for export), even if there is only one.
  (This maintains flexibility to add more later.)</li>
<li>Configuration related to the data itself (and therefore common across all
  sources) <strong>must</strong> be placed at the top-level of the request message.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> The configuration for import and export <strong>may</strong> be different from one
another. (For example, it would be sensible to import from a file but export to
a directory.)</p>
<h3 id="inline-sources">Inline sources</h3>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> also permit import and export "inline", where the contents to be
imported or exported are provided in the request or response.</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">InlineSource</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">books</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The source or destination <strong>should</strong> be named <code>InlineSource</code> or
  <code>InlineDestination</code>.</li>
<li>The message <strong>should</strong> include a repeated field representing the resource.
  However, if the resource structure is complex, the API <strong>may</strong> use a separate
  inline representation. In this situation, the same format <strong>must</strong> be used
  for both import and export.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="partial-failures">Partial failures</h3>
<p>While partial failures are normally discouraged, import and export RPCs
<strong>should</strong> include partial failure information in the metadata object. Each
individual error <strong>should</strong> be a <code>google.rpc.Status</code> object describing the
error. For more on errors, see <a href="/193">AIP-193</a>.</p>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-154</h4>
  <h1 id="resource-freshness-validation">Resource freshness validation</h1>
<p>APIs often need to validate that a client and server agree on the current state
of a resource before taking some kind of action on that resource. For example,
two processes updating the same resource in parallel could create a race
condition, where the latter process "stomps over" the effort of the former one.</p>
<p>ETags provide a way to deal with this, by allowing the server to send a
checksum based on the current content of a resource; when the client sends that
checksum back, the server can ensure that the checksums match before acting on
the request.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>A resource <strong>may</strong> include an <code>etag</code> field on any resource where it is
important to ensure that the client has an up to date resource before acting on
certain requests:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="c1">// A representation of a book.</span>
<span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Other fields...</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// This checksum is computed by the server based on the value of other</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// fields, and may be sent on update and delete requests to ensure the</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// client has an up-to-date value before proceeding.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">etag</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">99</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The etag field <strong>must</strong> be a string, and <strong>must</strong> be named <code>etag</code>.</li>
<li>The etag field on the <em>resource</em> <strong>should not</strong> be given any behavior
  annotations.</li>
<li>The etag field <strong>must</strong> be provided by the server on output, and values
  <strong>should</strong> conform to <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7232#section-2.3">RFC 7232</a>.</li>
<li>If a user sends back an etag which matches the current etag value, the
  service <strong>must</strong> permit the request (unless there is some other reason for
  failure).</li>
<li>If a user sends back an etag which does not match the current etag value, the
  service <strong>must</strong> send an <code>ABORTED</code> error response (unless another error takes
  precedence, such as <code>PERMISSION_DENIED</code> if the user is not authorized).</li>
<li>If the user does not send an etag value at all, the service <strong>should</strong> permit
  the request. However, services with strong consistency or parallelism
  requirements <strong>may</strong> require users to send etags all the time and reject the
  request with an <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code> error in this case.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> ETag values <strong>should</strong> include quotes as described in <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7232#section-2.3">RFC 7232</a>.
For example, a valid etag is <code>"foo"</code>, not <code>foo</code>.</p>
<h3 id="declarative-friendly-resources">Declarative-friendly resources</h3>
<p>A resource that is declarative-friendly (<a href="/128">AIP-128</a>) <strong>must</strong> include an <code>etag</code>
field.</p>
<h3 id="etags-on-request-methods">Etags on request methods</h3>
<p>In some situations, the etag needs to belong on a request message rather than
the resource itself. For example, an <code>Update</code> standard method can "piggyback"
off the <code>etag</code> field on the resource, but the <code>Delete</code> standard method can not:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">DeleteBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The name of the book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The current etag of the book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If an etag is provided and does not match the current etag of the book,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// deletion will be blocked and an ABORTED error will be returned.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">etag</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OPTIONAL</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>On a request message, the <code>etag</code> field <strong>should</strong> be given a behavior annotation
- either <code>REQUIRED</code> or <code>OPTIONAL</code>. See <a href="/203">AIP-203</a> for more information.</p>
<p>An <code>etag</code> field <strong>may</strong> also be used on custom methods, similar to the example
above.</p>
<h3 id="strong-and-weak-etags">Strong and weak etags</h3>
<p>ETags can be either "strongly validated" or "weakly validated":</p>
<ul>
<li>A strongly validated etag means that two resources bearing the same etag are
  byte-for-byte identical.</li>
<li>A weakly validated etag means that two resources bearing the same etag are
  equivalent, but may differ in ways that the service does not consider to be
  important.</li>
</ul>
<p>Resources <strong>may</strong> use either strong or weak etags, as it sees fit, but
<strong>should</strong> document the behavior. Additionally, weak etags <strong>must</strong> have a <code>W/</code>
prefix as mandated by <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7232#section-2.3">RFC 7232</a>.</p>
<h2 id="further-reading">Further reading</h2>
<ul>
<li>For how to retry on errors in client libraries, see <a href="/194">AIP-194</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2021-04-01</strong>: Updated an additional reference to <code>FAILED_PRECONDITION</code>
  to <code>ABORTED</code>.</li>
<li><strong>2021-03-05</strong>: Changed the etag error from <code>FAILED_PRECONDITION</code> (which
  becomes HTTP 400) to <code>ABORTED</code> (409).</li>
<li><strong>2020-10-06</strong>: Added declarative-friendly resource requirement.</li>
<li><strong>2020-09-02</strong>: Clarified that other errors may take precedence over
  <code>FAILED_PRECONDITION</code> for etag mismatches.</li>
<li><strong>2020-09-02</strong>: Add guidance for etags on request messages.</li>
<li><strong>2019-09-23</strong>: Changed the title to "resource freshness validation".</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-155</h4>
  <h1 id="request-identification">Request identification</h1>
<p>It is sometimes useful for an API to have a unique, customer-provided
identifier for particular requests. This can be useful for several purposes,
such as de-duplicating requests from parallel processes, ensuring the safety of
retries, or auditing.</p>
<p>The most important purpose for request IDs is to provide idempotency
guarantees: allowing the same request to be issued more than once without
subsequent calls having any effect. In the event of a network failure, the
client can retry the request, and the server can detect duplication and ensure
that the request is only processed once.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> add a <code>string request_id</code> parameter to request messages (including
those of standard methods) in order to uniquely identify particular requests.</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">CreateBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent resource where this book will be created.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The ID to use for the book, which will become the final component of</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// the book&#39;s resource name.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// This value should be 4-63 characters, and valid characters</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// are /[a-z][0-9]-/.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">book_id</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The book to create.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A unique identifier for this request. Restricted to 36 ASCII characters.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A random UUID is recommended.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// This request is only idempotent if a `request_id` is provided.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">request_id</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">UUID4</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>Providing a request ID <strong>must</strong> guarantee idempotency.<ul>
<li>If a duplicate request is detected, the server <strong>should</strong> return the
  response for the previously successful request, because the client most
  likely did not receive the previous response.</li>
<li>APIs <strong>may</strong> choose any reasonable timeframe for honoring request IDs.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The <code>request_id</code> field <strong>must</strong> be provided on the request message to which
  it applies (and it <strong>must not</strong> be a field on resources themselves).</li>
<li>Request IDs <strong>should</strong> be optional.</li>
<li>Request IDs <strong>should</strong> be able to be UUIDs, and <strong>may</strong> allow UUIDs to be the
  only valid format. The format restrictions for request IDs <strong>must</strong> be
  documented.<ul>
<li>Request IDs that are UUIDs <strong>must</strong> be annotated with the
  <code>google.api.FieldInfo.Format</code> value <code>UUID4</code> using the extension
  <code>(google.api.field_info).format = UUID4</code>. See <a href="/202">AIP-202</a> for more.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="stale-success-responses">Stale success responses</h3>
<p>In some unusual situations, it may not be possible to return an identical
success response. For example, a duplicate request to create a resource may
arrive after the resource has not only been created, but subsequently updated;
because the service has no other need to retain the historical data, it is no
longer feasible to return an identical success response.</p>
<p>In this situation, the method <strong>may</strong> return the current state of the resource
instead. In other words, it is permissible to substitute the historical success
response with a similar response that reflects more current data.</p>
<h2 id="further-reading">Further reading</h2>
<ul>
<li>For which codes to retry, see <a href="https://aip.dev/194">AIP-194</a>.</li>
<li>For how to retry errors in client libraries, see
  <a href="https://aip.dev/4221">AIP-4221</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="using-uuids-for-request-identification">Using UUIDs for request identification</h3>
<p>When a value is required to be unique, leaving the format open-ended can lead to
API consumers incorrectly providing a duplicate identifier. As such,
standardizing on a universally unique identifier drastically reduces the chance
for collisions when done correctly.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2024-01-08</strong>: Add book_id to request message.</li>
<li><strong>2023-10-02</strong>: Add UUID format extension guidance.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-156</h4>
  <h1 id="singleton-resources">Singleton resources</h1>
<p>APIs sometimes need to represent a resource where exactly one instance of the
resource always exists within any given parent. A common use case for this is
for a config object.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>An API <strong>may</strong> define <em>singleton resources</em>. A singleton resource <strong>must</strong>
always exist by virtue of the existence of its parent, with one and exactly one
per parent.</p>
<p>For example:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">Config</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;api.googleapis.com/Config&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pattern</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;users/{user}/config&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">singular</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;config&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">plural</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;configs&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// additional fields including name</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>The <code>Config</code> singleton would have the following RPCs:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">GetConfig</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">GetConfigRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Config</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">get</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{name=users/*/config}&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">UpdateConfig</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">UpdateConfigRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Config</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">patch</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{config.name=users/*/config}&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;config&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>Singleton resources <strong>must not</strong> have a user-provided or system-generated ID;
  their <a href="/122">resource name</a> includes the name of their parent followed by
  one static-segment.<ul>
<li>Example: <code>users/1234/config</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Singleton resources are always singular.<ul>
<li>Example: <code>users/1234/thing</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Singleton resource definitions <strong>must</strong> provide both the <code>singular</code> and
  <code>plural</code> fields (see above example).</li>
<li>Singleton resources <strong>may</strong> parent other resources.</li>
<li>Singleton resources <strong>must not</strong> define the <a href="/133"><code>Create</code></a> or
  <a href="/135"><code>Delete</code></a> standard methods. The singleton is implicitly created or
  deleted when its parent is created or deleted.</li>
<li>Singleton resources <strong>should</strong> define the <a href="/131"><code>Get</code></a> and
  <a href="/134"><code>Update</code></a> methods, and <strong>may</strong> define custom methods as
  appropriate.<ul>
<li>However, singleton resources <strong>must not</strong> define the <a href="/134"><code>Update</code></a>
  method if all fields on the resource are <a href="/203">output only</a>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Singleton resources <strong>may</strong> define the <a href="/132"><code>List</code></a> method, but <strong>must</strong>
  implement it according to <a href="/159">AIP-159</a>. See the example below.<ul>
<li>The trailing segment in the path pattern that typically represents the
  collection <strong>should</strong> be the <code>plural</code> form of the Singleton resource e.g.
  <code>/v1/{parent=users/*}/configs</code>.</li>
<li>If a parent resource ID is provided instead of the hyphen <code>-</code> as per
  <a href="/159">AIP-159</a>, then the service <strong>should</strong> return a collection of one Singleton
  resource corresponding to the specified parent resource.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ListConfigs</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ListConfigsRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ListConfigsResponse</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">get</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=users/*}/configs&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ListConfigsRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// To list all configs, use `-` as the user id.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Formats:</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// * `users/-`</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// * `users/{user}`</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Note: Specifying an actual user id will return a collection of one config.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Use GetConfig instead.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">child_type</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;api.googleapis.com/Config&quot;</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// other standard pagination fields...</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="support-for-standard-list">Support for Standard List</h3>
<p>While Singleton resources are not directly part of a collection themselves, they
can be viewed as part of their parent's collection. The one-to-one relationship
of parent-to-singleton means that for every one parent there is one singleton
instance, naturally enabling some collection-based methods when combined with
the pattern of <a href="/159">Reading Across Collections</a>. The Singleton can present
as a collection to the API consumer as it is indirectly one based on its parent.
Furthermore, presenting the Singleton resource as a pseudo-collection in such
methods enables future expansion to a real collection, should a Singleton be
found lacking.</p>
<h3 id="including-plural-definition">Including <code>plural</code> definition</h3>
<p>While a Singleton is by definition singular, there are certain cases where
a Singleton resource may appear in a plural form e.g., if the service supports
Standard List (as defined here). As such, it is better to forward declare the
plural form of the Singleton resource type than to not have it when needed.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2024-04-15:</strong> Singletons must specify <code>singular</code> and <code>plural</code> in resource.</li>
<li><strong>2023-08-10:</strong> Add Standard <code>List</code> support.</li>
<li><strong>2023-07-26:</strong> Clarified that read-only singletons should not have <code>Update</code>.</li>
<li><strong>2021-11-02:</strong> Added an example message and state parent eligibility.</li>
<li><strong>2021-01-14:</strong> Changed example from <code>settings</code> to <code>config</code> for clarity.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-157</h4>
  <h1 id="partial-responses">Partial responses</h1>
<p>Sometimes, a resource can be either large or expensive to compute, and the API
needs to give the user control over which fields it sends back.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> support partial responses in one of two ways:</p>
<h3 id="field-masks-parameter">Field masks parameter</h3>
<p>Field masks (<code>google.protobuf.FieldMask</code>) can be used for granting the user
fine-grained control over what fields are returned. An API <strong>should</strong> support the mask in a side channel.
For example, the parameter can be specified either using an HTTP query
parameter, an HTTP header, or a <a href="https://grpc.io/docs/what-is-grpc/core-concepts/#metadata">gRPC metadata entry</a>. Google Cloud APIs specify field masks as a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/apis/docs/system-parameters">system parameter</a>.</p>
<p>Field masks <strong>should not</strong> be specified in the <a href="/157#read-masks-as-a-request-field">request</a>.</p>
<ul>
<li>The value of the field mask parameter <strong>must</strong> be a <code>google.protobuf.FieldMask</code>.</li>
<li>The field mask parameter <strong>must</strong> be optional:<ul>
<li>An explicit value of <code>"*"</code> <strong>should</strong> be supported, and <strong>must</strong> return all
  fields.</li>
<li>If the field mask parameter is omitted, it <strong>must</strong> default to <code>"*"</code>, unless otherwise documented.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>An API <strong>may</strong> allow read masks with non-terminal repeated fields (unlike
  update masks), but is not obligated to do so.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Changing the default value of the field mask parameter is a <a href="/180#semantic-changes">breaking change</a>.</p>
<h3 id="view-enumeration">View enumeration</h3>
<p>Alternatively, an API <strong>may</strong> support partial responses with view enums.
View enums are useful for situations where an API only wants to expose a small
number of permutations to the user:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">enum</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BookView</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The default / unset value.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The API will default to the BASIC view.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="na">BOOK_VIEW_UNSPECIFIED</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Include basic metadata about the book, but not the full contents.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// This is the default value (for both ListBooks and GetBook).</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="na">BOOK_VIEW_BASIC</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Include everything.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="na">BOOK_VIEW_FULL</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The enum <strong>should</strong> be specified as a <code>view</code> field on the request message.</li>
<li>The enum <strong>should</strong> be named something ending in <code>-View</code></li>
<li>The enum <strong>should</strong> at minimum have values named <code>BASIC</code> and <code>FULL</code> (although
  it <strong>may</strong> have values other than these).</li>
<li>The <code>UNSPECIFIED</code> value <strong>must</strong> be valid (not an error), and the API
  <strong>must</strong> document what the unspecified value will do.<ul>
<li>For List RPCs, the effective default value <strong>should</strong> be <code>BASIC</code>.</li>
<li>For the following RPC types, the effective default value <strong>should</strong> be
  either <code>BASIC</code> or <code>FULL</code>:<ul>
<li>Get</li>
<li>Create</li>
<li>Update</li>
<li>Soft Delete</li>
<li>Custom Method</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The enum <strong>should</strong> be defined at the top level of the proto file (as it is
  likely to be needed in multiple requests, e.g. both <code>Get</code> and <code>List</code>). See
  <a href="/126">AIP-126</a> for more guidance on top-level enumerations.</li>
<li>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> add fields to a given view over time. APIs <strong>must not</strong> remove a
  field from a given view (this is a breaking change).</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> If a service requires (or might require) multiple views with
overlapping but distinct values, there is a potential for a namespace
conflict. In this situation, the service <strong>should</strong> nest the view enum within
the individual resource.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Having a partial response be the default of standard methods can
degrade the effectiveness of declarative clients. Providing a mechanism to
request the full resource be populated in the response, like this View
pattern, is preferred if partial responses are deemed necessary.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="read-masks-as-a-request-field">Read masks as a request field</h3>
<p><strong>Warning:</strong> Read mask as a single, explicit field on the request message is
<strong>DEPRECATED</strong> for Google APIs. The <a href="#field-masks-parameter">system parameter</a>
<strong>must</strong> be used instead. The following guidance is for the benefit of existing
legacy Google and external non-Google usage.</p>
<p>An API <strong>may</strong> support read masks as a single field on the request message:
<code>google.protobuf.FieldMask read_mask</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li>The read mask <strong>must</strong> be a <code>google.protobuf.FieldMask</code> and <strong>should</strong> be
  named <code>read_mask</code>.</li>
<li>The field mask <strong>should</strong> be optional:<ul>
<li>An explicit value of <code>"*"</code> <strong>should</strong> be supported, and <strong>must</strong> return all
  fields.</li>
<li>If the field mask parameter is not provided, all fields <strong>must</strong> be
  returned.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>An API <strong>may</strong> allow read masks with non-terminal repeated fields (unlike
  update masks), but is not obligated to do so.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="deprecating-read_mask-in-request-messages">Deprecating <code>read_mask</code> in request messages</h3>
<p>As mentioned, Google API infrastructure implements a service-wide response
field filtering mechanism, so there is no need for individual API methods to
specify a <code>read_mask</code> in their request schema. Doing so is both redundant and a
potential point of conflict for the client or service.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2025-10-03</strong>: Added default view guidance for other RPC types, and
                  declarative client warning.</li>
<li><strong>2025-06-16</strong>: Reinstate read mask guidance as historical/external reference.</li>
<li><strong>2023-05-09</strong>: Fix top-level enum example and link to <a href="/126">AIP-126</a>.</li>
<li><strong>2022-03-14:</strong> Updated guidance on default value and how to specify a read mask.</li>
<li><strong>2021-10-06:</strong> Updated the guidance with system parameters.</li>
<li><strong>2021-03-04:</strong> Added guidance for conflicting view enums.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-158</h4>
  <h1 id="pagination">Pagination</h1>
<p>APIs often need to provide collections of data, most commonly in the <a href="/132">List</a>
standard method. However, collections can often be arbitrarily sized, and also
often grow over time, increasing lookup time as well as the size of the
responses being sent over the wire. Therefore, it is important that collections
be paginated.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>RPCs returning collections of data <strong>must</strong> provide pagination <em>at the outset</em>,
as it is a <a href="#backwards-compatibility">backwards-incompatible change</a> to add
pagination to an existing method.</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="c1">// The request structure for listing books.</span>
<span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ListBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent, which owns this collection of books.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The maximum number of books to return. The service may return fewer than</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// this value.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If unspecified, at most 50 books will be returned.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The maximum value is 1000; values above 1000 will be coerced to 1000.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">int32</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">page_size</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A page token, received from a previous `ListBooks` call.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// When paginating, all other parameters provided to `ListBooks` must match</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// the call that provided the page token.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">page_token</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="c1">// The response structure from listing books.</span>
<span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ListBooksResponse</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The books from the specified publisher.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">books</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A token that can be sent as `page_token` to retrieve the next page.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this field is omitted, there are no subsequent pages.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">next_page_token</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>Request messages for collections <strong>should</strong> define an <code>int32 page_size</code>
  field, allowing users to specify the maximum number of results to return.<ul>
<li>The <code>page_size</code> field <strong>must not</strong> be required.</li>
<li>If the user does not specify <code>page_size</code> (or specifies <code>0</code>), the API
  chooses an appropriate default, which the API <strong>should</strong> document. The API
  <strong>must not</strong> return an error.</li>
<li>If the user specifies <code>page_size</code> greater than the maximum permitted by the
  API, the API <strong>should</strong> coerce down to the maximum permitted page size.</li>
<li>If the user specifies a negative value for <code>page_size</code>, the API <strong>must</strong>
  send an <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code> error.</li>
<li>The API <strong>may</strong> return fewer results than the number requested (including
  zero results), even if not at the end of the collection.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Request messages for collections <strong>should</strong> define a <code>string page_token</code>
  field, allowing users to advance to the next page in the collection.<ul>
<li>The <code>page_token</code> field <strong>must not</strong> be required.</li>
<li>If the user changes the <code>page_size</code> in a request for subsequent pages, the
  service <strong>must</strong> honor the new page size.</li>
<li>The user is expected to keep all other arguments to the RPC the same; if
  any arguments are different, the API <strong>should</strong> send an <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code>
  error.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The response <strong>must not</strong> be a streaming response.</li>
<li>Response messages for collections <strong>should</strong> define a
  <code>string next_page_token</code> field, providing the user with a page token that may
  be used to retrieve the next page.<ul>
<li>The field containing pagination results <strong>should</strong> be the first field in
  the message and have a field number of <code>1</code>. It <strong>should</strong> be a repeated
  field containing a list of resources constituting a single page of results.</li>
<li>If the end of the collection has been reached, the <code>next_page_token</code> field
  <strong>must</strong> be empty. This is the <em>only</em> way to communicate
  "end-of-collection" to users.</li>
<li>If the end of the collection has not been reached (or if the API can not
  determine in time), the API <strong>must</strong> provide a <code>next_page_token</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Response messages for collections <strong>may</strong> provide an <code>int32 total_size</code>
  field, providing the user with the total number of items in the list.<ul>
<li>This total <strong>may</strong> be an estimate (but the API <strong>should</strong> explicitly
  document that).</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="skipping-results">Skipping results</h3>
<p>The request definition for a paginated operation <strong>may</strong> define an <code>int32 skip</code>
field to allow the user to skip results.</p>
<p>The <code>skip</code> value <strong>must</strong> refer to the number of individual resources to skip,
not the number of pages.</p>
<p>For example:</p>
<ul>
<li>A request with no page token and a <code>skip</code> value of <code>30</code> returns a single page
  of results starting with the 31st result.</li>
<li>A request with a page token corresponding to the 51st result (because the
  first 50 results were returned on the first page) and a <code>skip</code> value of <code>30</code>
  returns a single page of results starting with the 81st result.</li>
</ul>
<p>If a <code>skip</code> value is provided that cannot be fulfilled e.g. due to latency of
querying a massive data set, the response <strong>must</strong> be <code>200 OK</code> with an empty
result set. If it is <em>known</em> to put the cursor beyond the total size of the
collection, the response <strong>must not</strong> include a <code>next_page_token</code>.</p>
<h3 id="opacity">Opacity</h3>
<p>Page tokens provided by APIs <strong>must</strong> be opaque (but URL-safe) strings, and
<strong>must not</strong> be user-parseable. This is because if users are able to
deconstruct these, <em>they will do so</em>. This effectively makes the implementation
details of your API's pagination become part of the API surface, and it becomes
impossible to update those details without breaking users.</p>
<p><strong>Warning:</strong> Base-64 encoding an otherwise-transparent page token is <strong>not</strong> a
sufficient obfuscation mechanism.</p>
<p>For page tokens which do not need to be stored in a database, and which do not
contain sensitive data, an API <strong>may</strong> obfuscate the page token by defining an
internal protocol buffer message with any data needed, and send the serialized
proto, base-64 encoded.</p>
<p>Page tokens <strong>must</strong> be limited to providing an indication of where to continue
the pagination process only. They <strong>must not</strong> provide any form of
authorization to the underlying resources, and authorization <strong>must</strong> be
performed on the request as with any other regardless of the presence of a page
token.</p>
<h3 id="expiring-page-tokens">Expiring page tokens</h3>
<p>Many APIs store page tokens in a database internally. In this situation, APIs
<strong>may</strong> expire page tokens a reasonable time after they have been sent, in
order not to needlessly store large amounts of data that is unlikely to be
used. It is not necessary to document this behavior.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> While a reasonable time may vary between APIs, a good rule of thumb
is three days.</p>
<h2 id="backwards-compatibility">Backwards compatibility</h2>
<p>Adding pagination to an existing RPC is a backwards-incompatible change. This
may seem strange; adding fields to proto messages is generally backwards
compatible. However, this change is <em>behaviorally</em> incompatible.</p>
<p>Consider a user whose collection has 75 resources, and who has already written
and deployed code. If the API later adds pagination fields, and sets the
default to 50, then that user's code breaks; it was getting all resources, and
now is only getting the first 50 (and does not know to advance pagination).
Even if the API set a higher default limit, such as 100, the user's collection
could grow, and <em>then</em> the code would break.</p>
<p>Additionally, <a href="https://google.aip.dev/client-libraries/4233">client libraries implement automatic
pagination</a>, typically representing paginated
RPCs using different method signatures to unpaginated ones. This means that
adding pagination to a previously-unpaginated method causes a breaking change
in those libraries.</p>
<p>For this reason, it is important to always add pagination to RPCs returning
collections <em>up front</em>; they are consistently important, and they can not be
added later without causing problems for existing users.</p>
<p><strong>Warning:</strong> This also entails that, in addition to presenting the pagination
fields, they <strong>must</strong> be <em>actually implemented</em> with a non-infinite default
value. Implementing an in-memory version (which might fetch everything then
paginate) is reasonable for initially-small collections.</p>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="degraded-skip-response">Degraded <code>skip</code> response</h3>
<p>Large collections, complex queries, and globally distributed data can all
contribute to a paginated method being unable to quickly or confidently fulfill
a given <code>skip</code> request. Backend queries can timeout, data collation can take
time, and the end user experience need not suffer as a result. In such cases,
the pagination interface can be leveraged to keep the client engaged by
providing a <code>next_page_token</code>, while the service collects an appropriate result.
When the service has definitively determined that the requested <code>skip</code> exceeds
the available results, the pagination interface is again applied and
<code>next_page_token</code> is omitted to signal the end of results.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2025-07-08</strong>: Clarify degraded skip response guidance</li>
<li><strong>2020-05-24</strong>: Clarified that adding pagination breaks client
  libraries.</li>
<li><strong>2020-05-13</strong>: Added guidance for skipping results.</li>
<li><strong>2020-08-24</strong>: Clarified that responses are not streaming responses.</li>
<li><strong>2020-06-24</strong>: Clarified that page size is always optional for users.</li>
<li><strong>2019-02-12</strong>: Added guidance on the field being paginated over.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
<li><strong>2019-07-19</strong>: Update the opacity requirement from "should" to "must".</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-159</h4>
  <h1 id="reading-across-collections">Reading across collections</h1>
<p>Sometimes, it is useful for a user to be able to retrieve resources across
multiple collections, or retrieve a single resource without needing to know
what collection it is in.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> support reading resources across multiple collections by allowing
users to specify a <code>-</code> (the hyphen or dash character) as a wildcard character
in a standard <a href="/132"><code>List</code></a> method:</p>
<div class="highlight language-None"><pre><span></span><code>GET /v1/publishers/-/books?filter=...
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The URI pattern <strong>must</strong> still be specified with <code>*</code> and permit the
  collection to be specified; a URI pattern <strong>must not</strong> hard-code the <code>-</code>
  character.</li>
<li>The method <strong>must</strong> explicitly document that this behavior is supported.</li>
<li>The resources provided in the response <strong>must</strong> use the canonical name of the
  resource, with the actual parent collection identifiers (instead of <code>-</code>).</li>
<li>Services <strong>may</strong> support reading across collections on <code>List</code> requests
  regardless of whether the identifiers of the child resources are guaranteed
  to be unique. However, services <strong>must not</strong> support reading across
  collections on <code>Get</code> requests if the child resources might have a collision.</li>
<li>Cross-parent requests <strong>should not</strong> support <code>order_by</code>. If they do, the
  field <strong>must</strong> document that it is best effort. This is because cross-parent
  requests introduce ambiguity around ordering, especially if there is
  difficulty reaching a parent (see <a href="/217">AIP-217</a>).</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Important:</strong> If listing across multiple collections introduces the
possibility of partial failures due to unreachable parents (such as when
listing across locations), the method <strong>must</strong> indicate this following the
guidance in <a href="/217">AIP-217</a>.</p>
<h3 id="unique-resource-lookup">Unique resource lookup</h3>
<p>Sometimes, a resource within a sub-collection has an identifier that is unique
across parent collections. In this case, it may be useful to allow a
<a href="/131"><code>Get</code></a> method to retrieve that resource without knowing which parent
collection contains it. In such cases, APIs <strong>may</strong> allow users to specify the
wildcard collection ID <code>-</code> (the hyphen or dash character) to represent any
parent collection:</p>
<div class="highlight language-None"><pre><span></span><code>GET https://example.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/-/books/{book}
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The URI pattern <strong>must</strong> still be specified with <code>*</code> and permit the
  collection to be specified; a URI pattern <strong>must not</strong> hard-code the <code>-</code>
  character.</li>
<li>The method <strong>must</strong> explicitly document that this behavior is supported.</li>
<li>The resource name in the response <strong>must</strong> use the canonical name of the
  resource, with actual parent collection identifiers (instead of <code>-</code>). For
  example, the request above returns a resource with a name like
  <code>publishers/123/books/456</code>, <em>not</em> <code>publishers/-/books/456</code>.</li>
<li>The resource ID <strong>must</strong> be unique within parent collections.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="further-reading">Further reading</h2>
<ul>
<li>For partial failures due to unreachable resources, see <a href="/217">AIP-217</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2019-08-26</strong>: Added a reference to guidance for unreachable resources.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
</ul>
