  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-160</h4>
  <h1 id="filtering">Filtering</h1>
<p>Often, when listing resources (using a list method as defined in <a href="/132">AIP-132</a> or
something reasonably similar), it is desirable to filter over the collection
and only return results that the user is interested in.</p>
<p>It is tempting to define a structure to handle the precise filtering needs for
each API. However, filtering requirements evolve frequently, and therefore it
is prudent to use a string field with a structured syntax accessible to a
non-technical audience. This allows updates to be able to be made
transparently, without waiting for UI or client updates.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Because list filters are intended for a potentially non-technical
audience, they sometimes borrow from patterns of colloquial speech rather than
common patterns found in code.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> provide filtering to users on <code>List</code> methods (or similar methods
to query a collection, such as <code>Search</code>). If they choose to do so, they
<strong>should</strong> follow the common specification for filters discussed here. The
syntax is formally defined in the <a href="/assets/misc/ebnf-filtering.txt">EBNF grammar</a>.</p>
<p>When employing filtering, a request message <strong>should</strong> have exactly one
filtering field, <code>string filter</code>. Filtering of related objects is handled
through <a href="#traversal-operator">traversal</a> or <a href="#functions">functions</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> List Filters have fuzzy matching characteristics with support for
result ranking and scoring. For developers interested in deterministic
evaluation of list filters, see <a href="https://github.com/google/cel-spec">CEL</a>.</p>
<h3 id="literals">Literals</h3>
<p>A bare literal value (examples: "42", "Hugo") is a value to be matched against.
Literals appearing alone (with no specified field) <strong>should</strong> usually be
matched anywhere it may appear in an object's field values.</p>
<p>However, a service <strong>may</strong> choose to only consider certain fields; if so, it
<strong>must</strong> document which fields it considers. A service <strong>may</strong> include new
fields over time, but <strong>should</strong> do so judiciously and consider impact on
existing users.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Literals separated by whitespace are considered to have a fuzzy
variant of <code>AND</code>. Therefore, <code>Victor Hugo</code> is roughly equivalent to
<code>Victor AND Hugo</code>.</p>
<h3 id="logical-operators">Logical Operators</h3>
<p>Filtering implementations <strong>should</strong> provide the binary operators:</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Operator</th>
<th>Example</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>AND</code></td>
<td><code>a AND b</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> and <code>b</code> are true.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>OR</code></td>
<td><code>a OR b OR c</code></td>
<td>True if any of <code>a</code>, <code>b</code>, <code>c</code> are true.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> To match common patterns of speech, the <code>OR</code> operator has higher
precedence than <code>AND</code>, unlike what is found in most programming languages. The
expression <code>a AND b OR c</code> evaluates: <code>a AND (b OR c)</code>. API documentation and
examples <strong>should</strong> encourage the use of explicit parentheses to avoid
confusion, but <strong>should not</strong> require explicit parentheses.</p>
<h3 id="negation-operators">Negation Operators</h3>
<p>Filtering implementations <strong>should</strong> provide the unary operators <code>NOT</code> and <code>-</code>.
These are used interchangeably, and a service that supports negation <strong>must</strong>
support both formats.</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Operator</th>
<th>Example</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>NOT</code></td>
<td><code>NOT a</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> is not true.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>-</code></td>
<td><code>-a</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> is not true.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h3 id="comparison-operators">Comparison Operators</h3>
<p>Filtering implementations <strong>should</strong> provide the binary comparison operators
<code>=</code>, <code>!=</code>, <code>&lt;</code>, <code>&gt;</code>, <code>&lt;=</code>, and <code>&gt;=</code> for string, numeric, timestamp, and
duration fields (but <strong>should not</strong> provide them for booleans or enums).</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Operator</th>
<th>Example</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>=</code></td>
<td><code>a = true</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> is true.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>!=</code></td>
<td><code>a != 42</code></td>
<td>True unless <code>a</code> equals 42.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>&lt;</code></td>
<td><code>a &lt; 42</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> is a numeric value below 42.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>a &gt; "foo"</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> is lexically ordered after "foo".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>&lt;=</code></td>
<td><code>a &lt;= "foo"</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> is "foo" or lexically before it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>&gt;=</code></td>
<td><code>a &gt;= 42</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> is a numeric value of 42 or higher.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Unlike in most programming languages, field names <strong>must</strong> appear on
the left-hand side of a comparison operator; the right-hand side only accepts
literals and logical operators.</p>
<p>Because filters are accepted as query strings, type conversion takes place to
translate the string to the appropriate strongly-typed value:</p>
<ul>
<li>Enums expect the enum's string representation (case-sensitive).</li>
<li>Booleans expect <code>true</code> and <code>false</code> literal values.</li>
<li>Numbers expect the standard integer or float representations. For floats,
  exponents are supported (e.g. <code>2.997e9</code>).</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/src/google/protobuf/duration.proto">Durations</a> expect a numeric representation followed by an <code>s</code> suffix (for
  seconds). Examples: <code>20s</code>, <code>1.2s</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/src/google/protobuf/timestamp.proto">Timestamps</a> expect an <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339">RFC-3339</a> formatted string (e.g.
  <code>2012-04-21T11:30:00-04:00</code>). UTC offsets are supported.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Warning:</strong> The identifiers <code>true</code>, <code>false</code>, and <code>null</code> only carry intrinsic
meaning when used in the context of a typed field reference.</p>
<p>Additionally, when comparing strings for equality, services <strong>should</strong> support
wildcards using the <code>*</code> character; for example, <code>a = "*.foo"</code> is true if <code>a</code>
<em>ends with</em> ".foo".</p>
<h3 id="traversal-operator">Traversal operator</h3>
<p>Filtering implementations <strong>should</strong> provide the <code>.</code> operator, which indicates
traversal through a message, map, or struct.</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Example</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>a.b = true</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> has a boolean <code>b</code> field that is true.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>a.b &gt; 42</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a</code> has a numeric <code>b</code> field that is above 42.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>a.b.c = "foo"</code></td>
<td>True if <code>a.b</code> has a string <code>c</code> field that is "foo".</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Traversal <strong>must</strong> be written using the field names from the resource. If a
service wishes to support "implicit fields" of some kind, they <strong>must</strong> do so
through well-documented <a href="#functions">functions</a>. A service <strong>may</strong> specify a
subset of fields that are supported for traversal.</p>
<p>If a user attempts to traverse to a field that is not defined on the message,
the service <strong>should</strong> return an error with <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code>. A service
<strong>may</strong> permit traversal to undefined keys on maps and structs, and <strong>should</strong>
document how it behaves in this situation.</p>
<p>When evaluating an expression involving a traversal, if any non-primitive field
in the chain is not set on the entry being evaluated, the entry <strong>should</strong> be
skipped i.e. not match the filter expression. This applies even when the
comparison is a <code>!=</code>, which would imply matching on empty values. In the
examples above, if resource field <code>a</code> is not set on the resource instance, that
instance is skipped as a non-match.</p>
<p><strong>Important:</strong> The <code>.</code> operator <strong>must not</strong> be used to traverse through a
repeated field or list, except for specific use with the <code>:</code> operator.</p>
<h3 id="has-operator">Has Operator</h3>
<p>Filtering implementations <strong>must</strong> provide the <code>:</code> operator, which means "has".
It is usable with collections (repeated fields or maps) as well as messages,
and behaves slightly differently in each case.</p>
<p>Repeated fields query to see if the repeated structure contains a matching
element:</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Example</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>r:42</code></td>
<td>True if <code>r</code> contains 42.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>r.foo:42</code></td>
<td>True if <code>r</code> contains an element <code>e</code> such that <code>e.foo = 42</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Important:</strong> Filters can not query a <em>specific</em> element on a repeated field
for a value. For example, <code>e.0.foo = 42</code> and <code>e[0].foo = 42</code> are <strong>not</strong> valid
filters.</p>
<p>Maps, structs, messages can query either for the presence of a field in the map
or a specific value:</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Example</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>m:foo</code></td>
<td>True if <code>m</code> contains the key "foo".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>m.foo:*</code></td>
<td>True if <code>m</code> contains the key "foo".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>m.foo:42</code></td>
<td>True if <code>m.foo</code> is 42.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>There are two slight distinctions when parsing messages:</p>
<ul>
<li>When traversing messages, a field is only considered to be present if it has
  a non-default value.</li>
<li>When traversing messages, field names are snake case, although
  implementations <strong>may</strong> choose to support automatic conversion between camel
  case and snake case.</li>
</ul>
<p>For all aforementioned types, simply checking for the presence of a top-level
resource field is possible with the <code>*</code> value:</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Example</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>r:*</code></td>
<td>True if <code>repeated</code> field <code>r</code> is present.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>p:*</code></td>
<td>True if <code>map</code> field <code>p</code> is present.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>m:*</code></td>
<td>True if <code>message</code> field <code>m</code> is present.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> For <code>map</code> and <code>repeated</code> fields, there is no semantic difference
between an unset field and "set with empty value" - they both resolve to "not
present".</p>
<h3 id="functions">Functions</h3>
<p>The filtering language supports a function call syntax in order to support
API-specific extensions. An API <strong>may</strong> define a function using the
<code>call(arg...)</code> syntax, and <strong>must</strong> document any specific functions it
supports.</p>
<h3 id="limitations">Limitations</h3>
<p>A service <strong>may</strong> specify further structure or limitations for filter queries,
above what is defined here. For example, a service may support the logical
operators but only permit a certain number of them (to avoid "queries of death"
or other performance concerns).</p>
<p>Further structure or limitations <strong>must</strong> be clearly documented, and
<strong>must not</strong> violate requirements set forth in this document.</p>
<h3 id="validation">Validation</h3>
<p>If a non-compliant or schematically invalid <code>filter</code> string is specified,
the API <strong>should</strong> error with <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code>. Wherever validation is relaxed
for <code>filter</code>, the API <strong>must</strong> document the difference.</p>
<p>Schematic validation refers, but is not limited to, the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>Fields referenced in the <code>filter</code> <strong>must</strong> exist on the filtered schema</li>
<li>Field values provided in the <code>filter</code> <strong>must</strong> align to the type of the field<ul>
<li>For example, for a field <code>int32 age</code> a <code>filter</code> like <code>"age=hello"</code> is
  invalid</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Field values for bounded data types e.g. <code>enum</code> provided in the <code>filter</code>
  <strong>must</strong> be a valid value in the set</li>
<li>Field values for standardized types e.g. <code>Timestamp</code> <strong>must</strong> conform to the
  documented standard (see <a href="#comparison-operators">Comparison Operators</a> for a
  list of such types)</li>
</ul>
<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->
<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-161</h4>
  <h1 id="field-masks">Field masks</h1>
<p>Often, when updating resources (using an update method as defined in <a href="/134">AIP-134</a> or
something reasonably similar), it is desirable to specify exactly which fields
are being updated, so that the service can ignore the rest, even if the user
sends new values.</p>
<p>It is tempting to define a mask format to handle the precise needs for each
API. However, masking requirements evolve, and therefore it is prudent to use a
structured syntax. This allows updates to be able to be made transparently,
without waiting for UI or client updates.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>These masks of field names are called "field masks". Fields representing a field
mask <strong>must</strong> use the <code>google.protobuf.FieldMask</code> type. Field masks are most
common on Update requests (<a href="/134">AIP-134</a>).</p>
<p>Field masks <strong>must</strong> always be relative to the resource:</p>
<p><strong>Warning:</strong> Read masks as a single field on the request message, for
example: <code>google.protobuf.FieldMask read_mask</code> are <strong>DEPRECATED</strong>. Instead, see
<a href="/157">AIP-157</a>.</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">UpdateBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The book to update.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The book&#39;s `name` field is used to identify the book to update.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The list of fields to update.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Fields are specified relative to the book</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// (e.g. `title`, `rating`; *not* `book.title` or `book.rating`).</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">google.protobuf.FieldMask</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">update_mask</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="read-write-consistency">Read-write consistency</h3>
<p>Read and write behavior for field masks <strong>must</strong> be self-consistent if a mask
is present:</p>
<ul>
<li>If a user updates a resource with a given mask, and then reads the same
  resource with the same mask, the exact same data <strong>must</strong> be returned.<ul>
<li>Exception: <a href="#output-only-fields">Output only fields</a>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Similarly, reading a resource with a given mask and then updating the
  resource with the returned data and the same mask <strong>must</strong> be a no-op.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> This implies that any mask that is valid for either read or write
<strong>must</strong> be valid for both.</p>
<h3 id="specifying-specific-fields">Specifying specific fields</h3>
<p>Field masks <strong>must</strong> permit the specification of specific fields in a defined
struct, using the <code>.</code> character for traversal.</p>
<p>Because field masks are always relative to the resource, direct fields on the
resource require no traversal (examples: <code>title</code>, <code>rating</code>). Traversal is used
when resources contain messages (example: <code>author.given_name</code>).</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> A user <strong>must</strong> be able to specify either a field as a whole, or one
of its subfields: <code>author</code> and <code>author.given_name</code> are both valid.</p>
<h3 id="map-fields">Map fields</h3>
<p>Field masks <strong>may</strong> permit the specification of specific fields in a map, if
and only if the map's keys are either strings or integers, using the <code>.</code>
character for traversal.</p>
<p>Field masks <strong>should</strong> support string keys that contain characters that are
problematic for the field mask syntax, using the backtick character.</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The name of the book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Reviews for the back cover. The key is the author of the review,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// and the value is the text of the review.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Valid field masks: reviews, reviews.smith, reviews.`John Smith`</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">map</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">reviews</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="wildcards">Wildcards</h3>
<p>Field masks <strong>may</strong> permit the use of the <code>*</code> character on a repeated field or
map to indicate the specification of particular sub-fields in the collection:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pattern</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The name of the book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">IDENTIFIER</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The author or authors of the book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Valid field masks: authors, authors.*.given_name, authors.*.family_name</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Invalid field masks: authors.0, authors.0.given_name</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Author</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">authors</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">Author</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The author&#39;s given name.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">given_name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The author&#39;s family name.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">family_name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Field masks <strong>must not</strong> permit accessing a particular element of a
repeated field by index, and <strong>must</strong> return an <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code> error if
this is attempted.</p>
<h3 id="output-only-fields">Output only fields</h3>
<p>If a user includes an output only field in an update mask indirectly (by using
a wildcard or specifying an overall message that includes an output-only
subfield), the service <strong>must</strong> ignore any output only fields provided as
input, even if they are cleared or modified.</p>
<p>If a user directly specifies an output only field in an update mask, the
service <strong>must</strong> ignore the output only fields provided as input, even if
they are cleared or modified, to permit the same field mask to be used for
input and output.</p>
<h3 id="invalid-field-mask-entries">Invalid field mask entries</h3>
<p>When reading data, field masks <strong>may</strong> ignore entries that point to a value
that can not exist (either a field that does not exist, or a map key that the
service considers invalid).</p>
<p>When writing data, field masks <strong>should</strong> return an <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code> error if
an entry points to a value that can not exist; however, the service <strong>may</strong>
permit deletions.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2023-10-18</strong>: Update guidance for presence of output only fields in update
  mask.</li>
<li><strong>2023-07-17</strong>: Move <code>update_mask</code> guidance to <a href="/134">AIP-134</a>.</li>
</ul>

  <p id="aip-state-banner" class="callout warning">
  This AIP is currently a draft. This means that it is being actively debated
  and discussed, and it may change in non-trivial ways.
</p>
  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-162</h4>
  <h1 id="resource-revisions">Resource Revisions</h1>
<p>Some APIs need to have resources with a revision history, where users can
reason about the state of the resource over time. There are several reasons for
this:</p>
<ul>
<li>Users may want to be able to roll back to a previous revision, or diff
  against a previous revision.</li>
<li>An API may create data which is derived in some way from a resource at a
  given point in time. In these cases, it may be desirable to snapshot the
  resource for reference later.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> We use the word <em>revision</em> to refer to a historical reference for a
particular resource, and intentionally avoid the term <em>version</em>, which refers
to the version of an API as a whole.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> store a revision history for a resource. Examples of when it is
useful include:</p>
<ul>
<li>When it is valuable to expose older versions of a resource via an API. This
  can avoid the overhead of the customers having to write their own API to store
  and enable retrieval of revisions.</li>
<li>Other resources depend on different revisions of a resource.</li>
<li>There is a need to represent the change of a resource over time.</li>
</ul>
<p>APIs implementing resources with a revision history <strong>should</strong> abstract resource
revisions as nested collection of the resource. Sometimes, the revisions
collection can be a top level collection, exceptions include:</p>
<ul>
<li>If resource revisions are meant to have longer lifespan than the parent
resource. In other words, resource revisions exist after resource deletion.</li>
</ul>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BookRevision</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The name of the book revision.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The snapshot of the book</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">snapshot</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OUTPUT_ONLY</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The timestamp that the revision was created.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="n">google.protobuf.Timestamp</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">create_time</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OUTPUT_ONLY</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Other revision IDs that share the same snapshot.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">alternate_ids</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OUTPUT_ONLY</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The <code>message</code> <strong>must</strong> be annotated as a resource (<a href="/123">AIP-123</a>).</li>
<li>The <code>message</code> name <strong>must</strong> be named <code>{ResourceType}Revision</code>.</li>
<li>The resource revision <strong>must</strong> contain a field with a message type of the
  parent resource, with a field name of <code>snapshot</code>.<ul>
<li>The value of <code>snapshot</code> <strong>must</strong> be the configuration of the parent
  at the point in time the revision was created.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The resource revision <strong>must</strong> contain a <code>create_time</code> field (see <a href="/142">AIP-142</a>).</li>
<li>The resource revision <strong>may</strong> contain a repeated field <code>alternate_ids</code>, which would
  contain a list of resource IDs that the revision is also known by (e.g. <code>latest</code>)</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="creating-revisions">Creating Revisions</h3>
<p>Depending on the resource, different APIs may have different strategies for</p>
<ul>
<li>Create a new revision any time that there is a change to the parent resource</li>
<li>Create a new revision when important system state changes</li>
<li>Create a new revision when specifically requested</li>
</ul>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> use any of these strategies. APIs <strong>must</strong>
document their revision creation strategy.</p>
<h3 id="resource-names-for-revisions">Resource names for revisions</h3>
<p>When referring to specific revision of a resource, the subcollection name
<strong>must</strong> be named <code>revisions</code>. Resource revisions have names with the format
<code>{resource_name}/revisions/{revision_id}</code>. For example:
<div class="highlight language-None"><pre><span></span><code>publishers/123/books/les-miserables/revisions/c7cfa2a8
</code></pre></div></p>
<h3 id="server-specified-aliases">Server-specified Aliases</h3>
<p>Services <strong>may</strong> reserve specific IDs to be <a href="/122#resource-id-aliases">aliases</a> (e.g.
<code>latest</code>). These are read-only and managed by the service.</p>
<div class="highlight language-None"><pre><span></span><code>GET /v1/publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}/revisions/{revision_id}
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>If a <code>latest</code> ID exists, it <strong>must</strong> represent the most recently created
revision. The content of <code>publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}/revisions/latest</code>
and <code>publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</code> can differ, as the latest revision may
be different from the current state of the resource.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="user-specified-aliases">User-Specified Aliases</h3>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> provide a mechanism for users to assign an <a href="/122#resource-id-aliases">alias</a> ID to an
existing revision with a custom method "alias":</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">AliasBookRevision</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">AliasBookRevisionRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{name=publishers/*/books/*/revisions/*}:alias&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">AliasBookRevisionRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/BookRevision&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The ID of the revision to alias to, e.g. `CURRENT` or a semantic</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// version.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">alias_id</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> have a <code>name</code> field:<ul>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> have a <code>alias_id</code> field:<ul>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If the user calls the method with an existing <code>alias_id</code>, the request <strong>must</strong>
  succeed and the alias will be updated to refer to the provided revision. This
  allows users to write code against a specific alias (e.g. <code>published</code>) and the
  revision can change with no code change.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="rollback">Rollback</h3>
<p>A common use case for a resource with a revision history is the ability to roll
back to a given revision. APIs <strong>should</strong> handle this with a <code>Rollback</code> custom
method:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RollbackBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RollbackBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BookRevision</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{name=publishers/*/books/*/revisions/*}:rollback&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The method <strong>must</strong> use the <code>POST</code> HTTP verb.</li>
<li>The method <strong>should</strong> return a resource revision.</li>
</ul>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">RollbackBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The revision that the book should be rolled back to.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/BookRevision&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> have a <code>name</code> field, referring to the resource
  revision whose configuration the resource should be rolled back to.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>must</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="child-resources">Child resources</h3>
<p>Resources with a revision history <strong>may</strong> have child resources. If they do,
there are two potential variants:</p>
<ul>
<li>Child resources where each child resource is a child of the parent resource
  as a whole.</li>
<li>Child resources where each child resource is a child of <em>a single revision
  of</em> the parent resource.</li>
</ul>
<p>APIs <strong>should not</strong> include multiple levels of resources with revisions, as
this quickly becomes difficult to reason about.</p>
<h3 id="standard-methods">Standard methods</h3>
<p>Any standard methods <strong>must</strong> implement the corresponding AIPs (<a href="/131">AIP-131</a>,
<a href="/132">AIP-132</a>, <a href="/133">AIP-133</a>, <a href="/134">AIP-134</a>, <a href="/135">AIP-135</a>), with the following additional behaviors:</p>
<ul>
<li>List methods: By default, revisions in the list response <strong>must</strong> be ordered
  in reverse chronological order. User can supply <code>order_by</code> to override the
  default behavior.</li>
<li>If the revision supports aliasing, a delete method with the resource name
  of the alias (e.g. <code>revisions/1.0.2</code>) <strong>must</strong> remove the alias instead of
  deleting the resource.</li>
</ul>
<p>As revisions are nested under the resource, also see <a href="/135#cascading-delete">cascading delete</a>.</p>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="abstract-revisions-as-nested-collection">Abstract revisions as nested collection</h3>
<p>Revisions being resources under nested collection make revisions a first class
citizen.</p>
<ul>
<li>Revisions can offer standard get, list, and delete methods.</li>
<li>It retains the flexibility of extending new fields to revision in addition to
  the resource message.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="tagging-to-aliases">Tagging to Aliases</h3>
<p>Previously, a concept of <code>tag</code> existed. This concept was redundant with that of
an <a href="/122#resource-id-aliases">alias</a>, and the terms were consolidated to reduce complexity in the AIPs.</p>
<h3 id="output-only-resource-configuration">Output only resource configuration</h3>
<p>Although it was an option to have the revision take in the resource
configuration as part of the create method, doing so would have allowed users to
submit resource configuration for a revision that the resource was never in.</p>
<p><code>OUTPUT_ONLY</code> and requiring that a created revision represents the resource at
current point in time eliminates that issue.</p>
<h2 id="history">History</h2>
<h3 id="switching-from-a-collection-extension-to-a-subcollection">Switching from a collection extension to a subcollection</h3>
<p>In 2023-09, revisions are abstracted as a nested resource collection. Prior to
this, revisions are more like extension of an existing resource by using <code>@</code>
symbol. List and delete revisions were custom methods on the resource
collection. A single Get method was used to retrieve either the resource
revision, or the resource.</p>
<p>Its primary advantage was allowing a resource reference to seamlessly refer to
a resource, or its revision.</p>
<p>It also had several disadvantages:</p>
<ul>
<li>List revisions is a custom method (:listRevisions) on the resource collection</li>
<li>Delete revision is a custom method on the resource collection</li>
<li>Not visible in API discovery doc</li>
<li>Resource ID cannot use <code>@</code></li>
</ul>
<p>The guidance was modified ultimately to enable revisions to behave like a
resource, which reduces the users cognitive load and allows resource-oriented
clients to easily list, get, create, and update revisions.</p>
<h3 id="using-resource-id-instead-of-tag">Using resource ID instead of tag</h3>
<p>In the previous design, revisions had a separate identifer for a revision known
as a <code>tag</code>, that would live in a revision.</p>
<p>Tags were effectively a shadow resource ID, requiring methods to create, get and
filter revisions based on the value of the tag.</p>
<p>By consolidating the concept of a tag into the revision ID, the user no longer
needs to be familiar with a second set of retrieval and identifier methods.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2023-09-01</strong>: AIP was updated to be a sub-collection.</li>
<li><strong>2021-04-27</strong>: Added guidance on returning the resource from Delete Revision.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-163</h4>
  <h1 id="change-validation">Change validation</h1>
<p>Occasionally, a user wants to validate an intended change to see what the
result will be before actually making the change. For example, a request to
provision new servers in a fleet will have an impact on the overall fleet size
and cost, and could potentially have unexpected downstream effects.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> provide an option to validate, but not actually execute, a
request, and provide the same response (status code, headers, and response
body) that it would have provided if the request was actually executed.</p>
<p>To provide this option, the method <strong>should</strong> include a <code>bool validate_only</code>
field in the request message:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ReviewBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">}];</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">int32</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">rating</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">comment</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If set, validate the request and preview the review, but do not actually</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// post it.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">bool</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">validate_only</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>The API <strong>must</strong> perform permission checks and any other validation that would
be performed on a "live" request; a request using <code>validate_only</code> <strong>must</strong> fail
if it determines that the actual request would fail.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> It may occasionally be infeasible to provide the full output. For
example, if creating a resource would create an auto-generated ID, it does not
make sense to do this on validation. APIs <strong>should</strong> omit such fields on
validation requests in this situation.</p>
<h3 id="declarative-friendly-resources">Declarative-friendly resources</h3>
<p>A resource that is declarative-friendly (<a href="/128">AIP-128</a>) <strong>must</strong> include a
<code>validate_only</code> field on methods that mutate the resource.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2020-10-06:</strong> Added declarative-friendly resource requirement.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-164</h4>
  <h1 id="soft-delete">Soft delete</h1>
<p>There are several reasons why a client could desire soft delete and undelete
functionality, but one over-arching reason stands out: recovery from mistakes.
A service that supports undelete makes it possible for users to recover
resources that were deleted by accident.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> support the ability to "undelete", to allow for situations where
users mistakenly delete resources and need the ability to recover.</p>
<p>If a resource needs to support undelete, the <code>Delete</code> method <strong>must</strong> simply
mark the resource as having been deleted, but not completely remove it from the
system. If the method behaves this way, it <strong>should</strong> return the updated
resource instead of <code>google.protobuf.Empty</code>.</p>
<p>Resources that support soft delete <strong>should</strong> have both a <code>delete_time</code> and
<code>purge_time</code> field as described in <a href="/148">AIP-148</a>. Additionally, resources <strong>should</strong>
include a <code>DELETED</code> state value if the resource includes a <code>state</code> field
(<a href="/216">AIP-216</a>).</p>
<h3 id="undelete">Undelete</h3>
<p>A resource that supports soft delete <strong>should</strong> provide an <code>Undelete</code> method:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">UndeleteBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">UndeleteBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{name=publishers/*/books/*}:undelete&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>POST</code>.</li>
<li>The <code>body</code> clause <strong>must</strong> be <code>"*"</code>.</li>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> be the resource itself. There is no
  <code>UndeleteBookResponse</code>.<ul>
<li>The response <strong>should</strong> include the fully-populated resource unless it is
  infeasible to do so.</li>
<li>If the undelete RPC is <a href="#long-running-undelete">long-running</a>, the response
  message <strong>must</strong> be a <code>google.longrunning.Operation</code> which resolves to the
  resource itself.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="undelete-request-message">Undelete request message</h3>
<p>Undelete methods implement a common request message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">UndeleteBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The name of the deleted book.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">type</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>name</code> field <strong>must</strong> be included. It <strong>should</strong> be called <code>name</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="long-running-undelete">Long-running undelete</h3>
<p>Some resources take longer to undelete a resource than is reasonable for a
regular API request. In this situation, the API <strong>should</strong> use a long-running
operation (<a href="/151">AIP-151</a>) instead:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">UndeleteBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">UndeleteBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{name=publishers/*/books/*}:undelete&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;OperationMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The response type <strong>must</strong> be set to the resource (what the return type would
  be if the RPC was not long-running).</li>
<li>Both the <code>response_type</code> and <code>metadata_type</code> fields <strong>must</strong> be specified.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="expunge">Expunge</h3>
<p>Resources that support soft delete <strong>may</strong> provide an <code>Expunge</code> custom method to
allow users to trigger immediate permanent deletion of a resource. This method can
operate on resources that are currently in a <code>CREATING</code>, <code>READY</code> or <code>SOFT_DELETED</code>
state (e.g., <code>delete_time</code> is set).</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="c1">// Permanently deletes a soft-deleted Book.</span>
<span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ExpungeBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ExpungeBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.protobuf.Empty</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{name=publishers/*/books/*}:expunge&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.method_signature</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;name&quot;</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The URI must use a custom method with the :expunge suffix.</li>
<li>The HTTP verb must be POST and the body clause must be "*".</li>
<li>The response message must be <code>google.protobuf.Empty</code> or a <code>google.longrunning.Operation</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="long-running-expunge">Long-running expunge</h3>
<p>If the expunge process takes significant time, the method <strong>may</strong> be a
<code>google.longrunning.Operation</code> (<a href="/151">AIP-151</a>) instead:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="c1">// Permanently deletes a soft-deleted Book.</span>
<span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ExpungeBook</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ExpungeBookRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{name=publishers/*/books/*}:expunge&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;google.protobuf.Empty&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;OperationMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.method_signature</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;name&quot;</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="expunge-request-message">Expunge request message</h3>
<p>Expunge methods implement a common request message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">ExpungeBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The name of the soft-deleted book to expunge.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">name</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">type</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> refer to the resource to be expunged by name.</li>
<li>There <strong>should not</strong> be any other request fields.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="list-and-get">List and Get</h3>
<p>Soft-deleted resources <strong>should not</strong> be returned in <code>List</code> (<a href="/132">AIP-132</a>) responses
by default (unless <code>bool show_deleted</code> is true). <code>Get</code> (<a href="/131">AIP-131</a>) requests for
soft-deleted resources <strong>should</strong> return the resource (rather than a
<code>NOT_FOUND</code> error).</p>
<p>APIs that soft delete resources <strong>may</strong> choose a reasonable strategy for
purging those resources, including automatic purging after a reasonable time
(such as 30 days), allowing users to set an expiry time (<a href="/214">AIP-214</a>), or retaining
the resources indefinitely. Regardless of what strategy is selected, the API
<strong>should</strong> document when soft deleted resources will be completely removed.</p>
<h3 id="declarative-friendly-resources">Declarative-friendly resources</h3>
<p>Soft-deletable resources have a poorer experience than hard-deleted resources in
declarative clients: since an ID on a soft-deleted resource is not re-usable
unless a custom method (undelete) is called, an imperative client must be
introduced or hand-written code is required to incorporate the usage of the
custom method.</p>
<h3 id="errors">Errors</h3>
<p>If the user does not have permission to access the resource, regardless of
whether or not it exists, the service <strong>must</strong> error with <code>PERMISSION_DENIED</code>
(HTTP 403). Permission <strong>must</strong> be checked prior to checking if the resource
exists.</p>
<p>If the user does have proper permission, but the requested resource does not
exist (either it was never created or already expunged), the service <strong>must</strong>
error with <code>NOT_FOUND</code> (HTTP 404).</p>
<p>If the user calling a soft <code>Delete</code> has proper permission, but the requested
resource is already deleted, the service <strong>must</strong> succeed if <code>allow_missing</code> is
<code>true</code>, and <strong>should</strong> error with <code>NOT_FOUND</code> (HTTP 404) if <code>allow_missing</code> is
<code>false</code>.</p>
<p>If the user calling <code>Undelete</code> has proper permission, but the requested
resource is not deleted, the service <strong>must</strong> respond with <code>ALREADY_EXISTS</code>
(HTTP 409).</p>
<p>If the user calling <code>Expunge</code> requests a resource that does not exist (was never
created or already expunged), the method <strong>must</strong> return <code>NOT_FOUND</code> (HTTP 404).</p>
<p>If the resource exists but is not in a ready or soft-deleted state, the method
<strong>must</strong> return <code>FAILED_PRECONDITION</code> (HTTP 400).</p>
<p>Standard permission errors (<code>PERMISSION_DENIED</code>) apply. Services <strong>must</strong> require
an explicit expunge permission that is separate from standard delete permissions
(e.g., <code>&lt;service&gt;.&lt;resource&gt;.expunge</code>).</p>
<h2 id="further-reading">Further reading</h2>
<ul>
<li>For the <code>Delete</code> standard method, see <a href="/135">AIP-135</a>.</li>
<li>For long-running operations, see <a href="/151">AIP-151</a>.</li>
<li>For resource freshness validation (<code>etag</code>), see <a href="/154">AIP-154</a>.</li>
<li>For change validation (<code>validate_only</code>), see <a href="/163">AIP-163</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2026-04-28</strong>: Added guidance for the <code>Expunge</code> custom method.</li>
<li><strong>2024-09-24</strong>: Included missing requirement for <code>delete_time</code>.</li>
<li><strong>2023-07-13</strong>: Renamed overloaded <code>expire_time</code> to <code>purge_time</code>.</li>
<li><strong>2021-07-12</strong>: Added error behavior when soft deleting a deleted resource.</li>
<li><strong>2021-07-12</strong>: Clarified that <code>ALREADY_EXISTS</code> errors apply to <code>Undelete</code>.</li>
<li><strong>2021-07-12</strong>: Changed the <code>expire_time</code> field to "should" for consistency
  with <a href="/148">AIP-148</a>.</li>
<li><strong>2020-09-23</strong>: Soft delete material in <a href="/135">AIP-135</a> migrated to this AIP.</li>
</ul>

      </li>
      
      <li class="glue-breadcrumbs__item" aria-level="2">
        <a class="glue-breadcrumbs__link" href="/general">
          General AIPs
        </a>
      </li>
      
      <li class="glue-breadcrumbs__item glue-breadcrumbs__item--active"
          aria-level="3">
        Criteria-based delete
      </li>
    </ol>
  </nav>
</section>
  
  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-165</h4>
  <h1 id="criteria-based-delete">Criteria-based delete</h1>
<p>Occasionally, an API may need to provide a mechanism to delete a large number
of resources based on some set of filter parameters, rather than requiring the
individual resource name of the resources to be deleted.</p>
<p>This is a rare case, reserved for situations where users need to delete
thousands or more resources at once, in which case the normal Batch Delete
pattern (<a href="/235">AIP-235</a>) becomes unwieldy and inconvenient.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p><strong>Important:</strong> Most APIs <strong>should</strong> use only Delete (<a href="/135">AIP-135</a>) or Batch
Delete (<a href="/235">AIP-235</a>) for deleting resources, and <strong>should not</strong> implement
deleting based on criteria. This is because deleting is generally irreversible
and this type of operation makes it easy for a user to accidentally lose
significant amounts of data.</p>
<p>An API <strong>may</strong> implement a Purge method to permit deleting a large number of
resources based on a filter string; however, this <strong>should</strong> only be done if
the Batch Delete (<a href="/235">AIP-235</a>) pattern is insufficient to accomplish the
desired goal:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PurgeBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">PurgeBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:purge&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;PurgeBooksResponse&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;PurgeBooksMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with the word <code>Purge</code>. The remainder of the
  RPC name <strong>should</strong> be the plural form of the resource being purged.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with a <code>Request</code> suffix.</li>
<li>The response type <strong>must</strong> be a <code>google.longrunning.Operation</code> (see
  <a href="/151">AIP-151</a>) that resolves to a message whose name matches the RPC name, with
  a <code>Response</code> suffix.</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>POST</code>, and the <code>body</code> <strong>must</strong> be <code>"*"</code>.</li>
<li>The URI path <strong>should</strong> represent the collection for the resource.</li>
<li>The <code>parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included in the URI. If the API wishes to
  support deletion across multiple parents, it <strong>should</strong> accept the <code>-</code>
  character consistent with <a href="/159">AIP-159</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>Purge methods implement a common request message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">PurgeBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The publisher to purge books from.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// To purge books across publishers, send &quot;publishers/-&quot;.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A filter matching the books to be purged.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">filter</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Actually perform the purge.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If `force` is set to false, the method will return a sample of</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// resource names that would be deleted.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">bool</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">force</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A singular <code>string parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included, unless the resource
  is top-level.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>A singular <code>string filter</code> field <strong>must</strong> be included and <strong>must</strong> follow the
  same semantics as in List methods (<a href="/160">AIP-160</a>).<ul>
<li>It <strong>should</strong> be <a href="/203">annotated as required</a>.</li>
<li>A wildcard value of <code>"*"</code> <strong>may</strong> be supported for deleting everything.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>A singular <code>bool force</code> field <strong>must</strong> be included. If it is not set, the API
  <strong>must</strong> return a count of the resources that would be deleted as well as a
  sample of those resources, without actually performing the deletion.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="response-message">Response message</h3>
<p>Purge methods implement a common response message pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">PurgeBooksResponse</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The number of books that this request deleted (or, if `force` is false,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// the number of books that will be deleted).</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">int32</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">purge_count</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A sample of the resource names of books that will be deleted.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Only populated if `force` is set to false.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">purge_sample</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">}];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A singular <code>int32 purge_count</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included, and provide the
  number of resources that were deleted (or would be deleted). This count
  <strong>may</strong> be an estimate similar to <code>total_size</code> in <a href="/158">AIP-158</a> (but the service
  <strong>should</strong> document this if so).</li>
<li>A <code>repeated string purge_sample</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included: If <code>force</code> is
  <code>false</code>, it <strong>should</strong> provide a sample of resource names that will be
  deleted. If <code>force</code> is true, this field <strong>should not</strong> be populated.<ul>
<li>The sample <strong>should</strong> be a sufficient size to catch clearly obvious
  mistakes: A good rule of thumb is 100. The API <strong>should</strong> document the
  size, and <strong>should</strong> document that it is a maximum (it is possible to send
  fewer).</li>
<li>The sample <strong>may</strong> be random or <strong>may</strong> be deterministic (such as the first
  matched resource names). The API <strong>should</strong> document which approach is
  used.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/123">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Even if <code>purge_count</code> and <code>purge_sample</code> are not included, the
<code>force</code> field <strong>must</strong> still be included in the request.</p>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2025-07-23:</strong> Explicitly state filter wildcard may be supported.</li>
<li><strong>2022-06-02:</strong> Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2020-10-29</strong>: Expanded guidance on HTTP, field behavior, and resource
  reference annotations.</li>
</ul>
