  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-231</h4>
  <h1 id="batch-methods-get">Batch methods: Get</h1>
<p>Some APIs need to allow users to get a specific set of resources at a
consistent time point (e.g. using a read transaction). A batch get method
provides this functionality.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> support Batch Get using the following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BatchGetBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchGetBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchGetBooksResponse</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">get</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:batchGet&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with <code>BatchGet</code>. The remainder of the RPC name
  <strong>should</strong> be the plural form of the resource being retrieved.</li>
<li>The request and response messages <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with
  <code>Request</code> and <code>Response</code> suffixes.</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>GET</code>.</li>
<li>The HTTP URI <strong>must</strong> end with <code>:batchGet</code>.</li>
<li>The URI path <strong>should</strong> represent the collection for the resource, matching
  the collection used for simple CRUD operations. If the operation spans
  parents, a dash (<code>-</code>) <strong>may</strong> be accepted as a wildcard.</li>
<li>There <strong>must not</strong> be a body key in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation.</li>
<li>The operation <strong>must</strong> be atomic: it <strong>must</strong> fail for all resources or
  succeed for all resources (no partial success). For situations requiring
  partial failures, <code>List</code> (<a href="https://aip.dev/132">AIP-132</a>) methods <strong>should</strong> be used.<ul>
<li>If the operation covers multiple locations and at least one location is
  down, the operation <strong>must</strong> fail.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>The request for a batch get method <strong>should</strong> be specified with the following
pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchGetBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent resource shared by all books being retrieved.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this is set, the parent of all of the books specified in `names`</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// must match this field.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The names of the books to retrieve.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A maximum of 1000 books can be retrieved in a batch.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">names</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included, unless the resource being retrieved
  is a top-level resource, to facilitate inclusion in the URI as
  well to permit a single permissions check. If a caller sets this field, and
  the parent collection in the name of any resource being retrieved does not
  match, the request <strong>must</strong> fail.<ul>
<li>This field <strong>should</strong> be required if only 1 parent per request is allowed.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/122#fields-representing-a-resources-parent">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> include a repeated field which accepts the
  resource names specifying the resources to retrieve. The field <strong>should</strong> be
  named <code>names</code>.<ul>
<li>If no resource names are provided, the API <strong>should</strong> error with
  <code>INVALID_ARGUMENT</code>.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be required.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/122#fields-representing-resource-names">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Other fields besides <code>name</code> <strong>may</strong> be "hoisted" from the <a href="/131#request-message">standard Get
  request</a>. There is no way to allow for these fields to
  accept different values for different resources; if this is needed, use the
  <a href="#nested-request-objects">alternative request message form</a>.</li>
<li>Batch get <strong>should not</strong> support pagination because transactionality across
  API calls would be extremely difficult to implement or enforce, and the
  request defines the exact scope of the response anyway.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
<li>The comment above the <code>names</code> field <strong>should</strong> document the maximum number of
  requests allowed.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="response-message">Response message</h3>
<p>The response for a batch get method <strong>should</strong> be specified with the following
pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchGetBooksResponse</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Books requested.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">books</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> include one repeated field corresponding to the
  resources being retrieved.</li>
<li>The order of books in the response <strong>must</strong> be the same as the names in the
  request.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="nested-request-objects">Nested request objects</h3>
<p>If the <a href="/131#request-message">standard Get request message</a> contains a field besides
the resource name that needs to be different between different resources being
requested, the batch message <strong>may</strong> alternatively hold a <code>repeated</code> field of
the <a href="/131#request-message">standard Get request message</a>. This is generally
discouraged unless your use case really requires it.</p>
<p>The request for a batch get method using this approach <strong>should</strong> be specified
with the following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchGetBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent resource shared by all books being retrieved.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this is set, the parent field in the GetBookRequest messages</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// must either be empty or match this field.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The requests specifying the books to retrieve.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A maximum of 1000 books can be retrieved in a batch.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">GetBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">requests</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included. If a caller sets this field, and the
  parent collection in the name of any resource being retrieved does not match,
  the request <strong>must</strong> fail.<ul>
<li>This field <strong>should</strong> be required if only 1 parent per request is allowed.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/122#fields-representing-a-resources-parent">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> include a repeated field which accepts the
  request messages specifying the resources to retrieve, as specified for
  <a href="/131#request-message">standard Get methods</a>. The field <strong>should</strong> be named
  <code>requests</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be required.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Other fields <strong>may</strong> be "hoisted" from the <a href="/131#request-message">standard Get
  request</a>, which means that the field can be set at either
  the batch level or child request level. Similar to <code>parent</code>, if both the
  batch level and child request level are set for the same field, the values
  <strong>must</strong> match.</li>
<li>Batch get <strong>should not</strong> support pagination because transactionality across
  API calls would be extremely difficult to implement or enforce, and the
  request defines the exact scope of the response anyway.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
<li>The comment above the <code>requests</code> field <strong>should</strong> document the maximum number
  of requests allowed.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2022-06-02:</strong> Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2020-09-16</strong>: Suggested annotating <code>parent</code>, <code>names</code>, and <code>requests</code> fields.</li>
<li><strong>2020-08-27</strong>: Removed parent recommendations for top-level resources.</li>
<li><strong>2020-03-24</strong>: Clarified behavior if no resource names are sent.</li>
<li><strong>2019-09-11</strong>: Changed the primary recommendation to specify a repeated
  string instead of a repeated standard Get request message. Moved the original
  recommendation into its own section.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-233</h4>
  <h1 id="batch-methods-create">Batch methods: Create</h1>
<p>Some APIs need to allow users to create multiple resources in a single
transaction. A batch create method provides this functionality.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> support Batch Create using the following two patterns:</p>
<p>Returning the response synchronously</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BatchCreateBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchCreateBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchCreateBooksResponse</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:batchCreate&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>Returning an Operation which resolves to the response asynchronously</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BatchCreateBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchCreateBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:batchCreate&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;BatchCreateBooksResponse&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;BatchCreateBooksOperationMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with <code>BatchCreate</code>. The remainder of the RPC
  name <strong>should</strong> be the plural form of the resource being created.</li>
<li>The request and response messages <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with
  <code>Request</code> and <code>Response</code> suffixes.</li>
<li>If the batch method returns an <code>google.longrunning.Operation</code>, both the
  <code>response_type</code> and <code>metadata_type</code> fields <strong>must</strong> be specified.</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>POST</code>.</li>
<li>The HTTP URI <strong>must</strong> end with <code>:batchCreate</code>.</li>
<li>The URI path <strong>should</strong> represent the collection for the resource, matching
  the collection used for simple CRUD operations. If the operation spans
  parents, a dash (<code>-</code>) <strong>may</strong> be accepted as a wildcard.</li>
<li>The body clause in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation <strong>should</strong> be <code>"*"</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="atomic-vs-partial-success">Atomic vs. Partial Success</h3>
<ul>
<li>The batch create method <strong>may</strong> support atomic (all resources created or none
  are) or partial success behavior. To make a choice, consider the following
  factors:<ul>
<li><strong>Complexity of Ensuring Atomicity:</strong> Operations that are simple
  passthrough database transactions <strong>should</strong> use an atomic operation,
  while operations that manage complex resources <strong>should</strong> use partial
  success operations.</li>
<li><strong>End-User Experience:</strong> Consider the perspective of the API consumer.
  Would atomic behavior be preferable for the given use case, even if it
  means that a large batch could fail due to issues with a single or a few
  entries?</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Synchronous batch create <strong>must</strong> be atomic.</li>
<li>Asynchronous batch create <strong>may</strong> support atomic or partial success.<ul>
<li>If supporting partial success, see
  <a href="#operation-metadata-message">Operation metadata message</a> requirements.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>The request for a batch create method <strong>should</strong> be specified with the
following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchCreateBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent resource shared by all books being created.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this is set, the parent field in the CreateBookRequest messages</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// must either be empty or match this field.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The request message specifying the resources to create.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A maximum of 1000 books can be created in a batch.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">CreateBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">requests</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included, unless the resource being created is
  a top-level resource. If a caller sets this field, and the
  <code>parent</code> field of any child request message does not match, the request
  <strong>must</strong> fail. The <code>parent</code> field of child request messages can be omitted if
  the <code>parent</code> field in this request is set.<ul>
<li>This field <strong>should</strong> be required if only 1 parent per request is allowed.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/122#fields-representing-a-resources-parent">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> include a repeated field which accepts the
  request messages specifying the resources to create, as specified for
  <a href="/133#request-message">standard Create methods</a>. The field <strong>should</strong> be named
  <code>requests</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be required.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Other fields <strong>may</strong> be "hoisted" from the <a href="/133#request-message">standard Create
  request</a>, which means that the field can be set at either
  the batch level or child request level. Similar to <code>parent</code>, if both the
  batch level and child request level are set for the same field, the values
  <strong>must</strong> match.<ul>
<li>Fields which must be unique cannot be hoisted (e.g. Customer-provided id
  fields).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
<li>The comment above the <code>requests</code> field <strong>should</strong> document the maximum number
  of requests allowed.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="response-message">Response message</h3>
<p>The response for a batch create method <strong>should</strong> be specified with the
following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchCreateBooksResponse</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Books created.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">books</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> include one repeated field corresponding to the
  resources that were created.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="operation-metadata-message">Operation metadata message</h3>
<ul>
<li>The <code>metadata_type</code> message <strong>must</strong> either match the RPC name with
  <code>OperationMetadata</code> suffix, or be named with <code>Batch</code> prefix and
  <code>OperationMetadata</code> suffix if the type is shared by multiple Batch methods.</li>
<li>If batch create method supports partial success, the metadata message <strong>must</strong>
  include a <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field to communicate
  the partial failures.<ul>
<li>The key in this map is the index of the request in the <code>requests</code> field in
  the batch request.</li>
<li>The value in each map entry <strong>must</strong> mirror the error(s) that would normally
  be returned by the singular Standard Create method.</li>
<li>If a failed request can eventually succeed due to server side retries, such
  transient errors <strong>must not</strong> be communicated using <code>failed_requests</code>.</li>
<li>When all requests in the batch fail, <code>Operation.error</code> <strong>must</strong> be set with
  <code>code = google.rpc.Code.Aborted</code> and <code>message = "None of the requests
  succeeded, refer to the BatchCreateBooksOperationMetadata.failed_requests
  for individual error details"</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The metadata message <strong>may</strong> include other fields to communicate the
  operation progress.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="adopting-partial-success">Adopting Partial Success</h3>
<p>In order for an existing Batch API to adopt the partial success pattern, the API
must do the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>The default behavior must be retained to avoid incompatible behavioral
  changes.</li>
<li>If the API returns an Operation:<ul>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> have a <code>bool return_partial_success</code> field.</li>
<li>The Operation <code>metadata_type</code> <strong>must</strong> include a
  <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field.</li>
<li>When the <code>bool return_partial_success</code> field is set to true in a request,
  the API should allow partial success behavior, otherwise it should continue
  with atomic behavior as default.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If the API returns a direct response synchronously:<ul>
<li>Since the existing clients will treat a success response as an atomic
  operation, the existing version of the API <strong>must not</strong> adopt the partial
  success pattern.</li>
<li>A new version <strong>must</strong> be created instead that returns an Operation and
  follows the partial success pattern described in this AIP.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="restricting-synchronous-batch-methods-to-be-atomic">Restricting synchronous batch methods to be atomic</h3>
<p>The restriction that synchronous batch methods must be atomic is a result of
the following considerations.</p>
<p>The previous iteration of this AIP recommended batch methods must be atomic.
There is no clear way to convey partial failure in a sync response status code
because an OK implies it all worked. Therefore, adding a new field to the
response to indicate partial failure would be a breaking change because the
existing clients would interpret an OK response as all resources created.</p>
<p>On the other hand, as described in <a href="https://aip.dev/193">AIP-193</a>, Operations
are more capable of presenting partial states. The response status code for an
Operation does not convey anything about the outcome of the underlying operation
and a client has to check the response body to determine if the operation was
successful.</p>
<h3 id="communicating-partial-failures">Communicating partial failures</h3>
<p>The AIP recommends using a <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field
to communicate partial failures, where the key is the index of the failed
request in the original batch request. The other options considered were:</p>
<ul>
<li>A <code>repeated google.rpc.Status</code> field. This was rejected because it is not
  clear which entry corresponds to which request.</li>
<li>A <code>map&lt;string, google.rpc.Status&gt;</code> field, where the key is the request id of
  the failed request. This was rejected because:<ul>
<li>Client will need to maintain a map of request_id -&gt; request in order to use
  the partial success response.</li>
<li>Populating a request id for the purpose of communicating errors could
  conflict with <a href="https://aip.dev/155">AIP-155</a> if the service can not
  guarantee idempotency for an individual request across multiple batch
  requests.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>A <code>repeated FailedRequest</code> field, where FailedRequest contains the individual
  create request and the <code>google.rpc.Status</code>. This was rejected because echoing
  the request payload back in response is discouraged due to additional
  challenges around user data sensitivity.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2025-03-06</strong>: Added detailed guidance for partial success behavior, and
  decision framework for choosing between atomic and partial success</li>
<li><strong>2023-04-18</strong>: Changed the recommendation to allow returning partial 
  successes.</li>
<li><strong>2022-06-02</strong>: Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2020-09-16</strong>: Suggested annotating <code>parent</code> and <code>requests</code> fields.</li>
<li><strong>2020-08-27</strong>: Removed parent recommendations for top-level resources.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-234</h4>
  <h1 id="batch-methods-update">Batch methods: Update</h1>
<p>Some APIs need to allow users to modify a set of resources in a single
transaction. A batch update method provides this functionality.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> support Batch Update using the following two patterns:</p>
<p>Returning the response synchronously</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BatchUpdateBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchUpdateBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchUpdateBooksResponse</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:batchUpdate&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>Returning an Operation which resolves to the response asynchronously</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BatchUpdateBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchUpdateBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:batchUpdate&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;BatchUpdateBooksResponse&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;BatchUpdateBooksOperationMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with <code>BatchUpdate</code>. The remainder of the RPC
  name <strong>should</strong> be the plural form of the resource being updated.</li>
<li>The request and response messages <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with
  <code>Request</code> and <code>Response</code> suffixes.</li>
<li>If the batch method returns an <code>google.longrunning.Operation</code>, both the
  <code>response_type</code> and <code>metadata_type</code> fields <strong>must</strong> be specified.</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>POST</code>.</li>
<li>The HTTP URI <strong>must</strong> end with <code>:batchUpdate</code>.</li>
<li>The URI path <strong>should</strong> represent the collection for the resource, matching
  the collection used for simple CRUD operations. If the operation spans
  parents, a dash (<code>-</code>) <strong>may</strong> be accepted as a wildcard.</li>
<li>The body clause in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation <strong>should</strong> be <code>"*"</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="atomic-vs-partial-success">Atomic vs. Partial Success</h3>
<ul>
<li>The batch update method <strong>may</strong> support atomic (all resources updated or none
  are) or partial success behavior. To make a choice, consider the following
  factors:<ul>
<li><strong>Complexity of Ensuring Atomicity:</strong> Operations that are simple
  passthrough database transactions <strong>should</strong> use an atomic operation,
  while operations that manage complex resources <strong>should</strong> use partial
  success operations.</li>
<li><strong>End-User Experience:</strong> Consider the perspective of the API consumer.
  Would atomic behavior be preferable for the given use case, even if it
  means that a large batch could fail due to issues with a single or a few
  entries?</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Synchronous batch update <strong>must</strong> be atomic.</li>
<li>Asynchronous batch update <strong>may</strong> support atomic or partial success.<ul>
<li>If supporting partial success, see
  <a href="#operation-metadata-message">Operation metadata message</a> requirements.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>The request for a batch update method <strong>should</strong> be specified with the
following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchUpdateBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent resource shared by all books being updated.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this is set, the parent field in the UpdateBookRequest messages</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// must either be empty or match this field.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The request message specifying the resources to update.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A maximum of 1000 books can be modified in a batch.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">UpdateBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">requests</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included, unless the resource being updated is
  a top-level resource. If a caller sets this field, and the
  parent collection in the name of any resource being updated does not match,
  the request <strong>must</strong> fail.<ul>
<li>This field <strong>should</strong> be required if only 1 parent per request is allowed.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/122#fields-representing-a-resources-parent">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> include a repeated field which accepts the
  request messages specifying the resources to update, as specified for
  <a href="/134#request-message">standard Update methods</a>. The field <strong>should</strong> be named
  <code>requests</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be required.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Other fields <strong>may</strong> be "hoisted" from the <a href="/134#request-message">standard Update
  request</a>, which means that the field can be set at either
  the batch level or child request level. Similar to <code>parent</code>, if both the
  batch level and child request level are set for the same field, the values
  <strong>must</strong> match.<ul>
<li>The <code>update_mask</code> field is a good candidate for hoisting.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
<li>The comment above the <code>requests</code> field <strong>should</strong> document the maximum number of
  requests allowed.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="response-message">Response message</h3>
<p>The response for a batch update method <strong>should</strong> be specified with the
following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchUpdateBooksResponse</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Books updated.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">books</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> include one repeated field corresponding to the
  resources that were updated.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="operation-metadata-message">Operation metadata message</h3>
<ul>
<li>The <code>metadata_type</code> message <strong>must</strong> either match the RPC name with
  <code>OperationMetadata</code> suffix, or be named with <code>Batch</code> prefix and
  <code>OperationMetadata</code> suffix if the type is shared by multiple Batch methods.</li>
<li>If batch update method supports partial success, the metadata message <strong>must</strong>
  include a <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field to communicate
  the partial failures.<ul>
<li>The key in this map is the index of the request in the <code>requests</code> field
  in the batch request.</li>
<li>The value in each map entry <strong>must</strong> mirror the error(s) that would normally
  be returned by the singular Standard Update method.</li>
<li>If a failed request can eventually succeed due to server side retries, such
  transient errors <strong>must not</strong> be communicated using <code>failed_requests</code>.</li>
<li>When all requests in the batch fail, <code>Operation.error</code> <strong>must</strong> be set with
  <code>code = google.rpc.Code.Aborted</code> and <code>message = "None of the requests
  succeeded, refer to the BatchUpdateBooksOperationMetadata.failed_requests
  for individual error details"</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The metadata message <strong>may</strong> include other fields to communicate the
  operation progress.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="adopting-partial-success">Adopting Partial Success</h3>
<p>In order for an existing Batch API to adopt the partial success pattern, the API
must do the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>The default behavior must be retained to avoid incompatible behavioral
  changes.</li>
<li>If the API returns an Operation:<ul>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> have a <code>bool return_partial_success</code> field.</li>
<li>The Operation <code>metadata_type</code> <strong>must</strong> include a
  <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field.</li>
<li>When the <code>bool return_partial_success</code> field is set to true in a request,
  the API should allow partial success behavior, otherwise it should continue
  with atomic behavior as default.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If the API returns a direct response synchronously:<ul>
<li>Since the existing clients will treat a success response as an atomic
  operation, the existing version of the API <strong>must not</strong> adopt the partial
  success pattern.</li>
<li>A new version <strong>must</strong> be created instead that returns an Operation and
  follows the partial success pattern described in this AIP.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="restricting-synchronous-batch-methods-to-be-atomic">Restricting synchronous batch methods to be atomic</h3>
<p>The restriction that synchronous batch methods must be atomic is a result of
the following considerations.</p>
<p>The previous iteration of this AIP recommended batch methods must be atomic.
There is no clear way to convey partial failure in a sync response status code
because an OK implies it all worked. Therefore, adding a new field to the
response to indicate partial failure would be a breaking change because the
existing clients would interpret an OK response as all resources updated.</p>
<p>On the other hand, as described in <a href="https://aip.dev/193">AIP-193</a>, Operations
are more capable of presenting partial states. The response status code for an
Operation does not convey anything about the outcome of the underlying operation
and a client has to check the response body to determine if the operation was
successful.</p>
<h3 id="communicating-partial-failures">Communicating partial failures</h3>
<p>The AIP recommends using a <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field
to communicate partial failures, where the key is the index of the failed
request in the original batch request. The other options considered were:</p>
<ul>
<li>A <code>repeated google.rpc.Status</code> field. This was rejected because it is not
  clear which entry corresponds to which request.</li>
<li>A <code>map&lt;string, google.rpc.Status&gt;</code> field, where the key is the request id of
  the failed request. This was rejected because:<ul>
<li>Client will need to maintain a map of request_id -&gt; request in order to use
  the partial success response.</li>
<li>Populating a request id for the purpose of communicating errors could
  conflict with <a href="https://aip.dev/155">AIP-155</a> if the service can not
  guarantee idempotency for an individual request across multiple batch
  requests.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>A <code>repeated FailedRequest</code> field, where FailedRequest contains the individual
  update request and the <code>google.rpc.Status</code>. This was rejected because echoing
  the request payload back in response is discouraged due to additional
  challenges around user data sensitivity.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2025-03-06</strong>: Changed recommendation to allow partial success, along with
  detailed guidance</li>
<li><strong>2022-06-02:</strong> Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2020-09-16</strong>: Suggested annotating <code>parent</code> and <code>requests</code> fields.</li>
<li><strong>2020-08-27</strong>: Removed parent recommendations for top-level resources.</li>
<li><strong>2019-09-11</strong>: Fixed the wording about which child field the <code>parent</code> field
  should match.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
</ul>

  <h4 class="aip-number">AIP-235</h4>
  <h1 id="batch-methods-delete">Batch methods: Delete</h1>
<p>Some APIs need to allow users to delete a set of resources in a single
transaction. A batch delete method provides this functionality.</p>
<h2 id="guidance">Guidance</h2>
<p>APIs <strong>may</strong> support Batch Delete using the following two patterns:</p>
<p>Returning the response synchronously</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BatchDeleteBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchDeleteBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.protobuf.Empty</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:batchDelete&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>Returning an Operation which resolves to the response asynchronously</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">rpc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BatchDeleteBooks</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BatchDeleteBooksRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k">returns</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.Operation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.http</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">post</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;/v1/{parent=publishers/*}/books:batchDelete&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">body</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;*&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">option</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.longrunning.operation_info</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">response_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;google.protobuf.Empty&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="n">metadata_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;BatchDeleteBooksOperationMetadata&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">};</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The RPC's name <strong>must</strong> begin with <code>BatchDelete</code>. The remainder of the RPC
  name <strong>should</strong> be the plural form of the resource being deleted.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> match the RPC name, with a <code>Request</code> suffix.</li>
<li>The response message <strong>should</strong> be <code>google.protobuf.Empty</code>.<ul>
<li>If the resource is <a href="/135#soft-delete">soft deleted</a>, the response message
  <strong>should</strong> be a response message containing the updated resources.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If the batch method returns an <code>google.longrunning.Operation</code>, both the
  <code>response_type</code> and <code>metadata_type</code> fields <strong>must</strong> be specified.<ul>
<li>If the resource is <a href="/135#soft-delete">soft deleted</a>, the <code>response_type</code>
  <strong>should</strong> be a response message containing the updated resources.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The HTTP verb <strong>must</strong> be <code>POST</code> (not <code>DELETE</code>).</li>
<li>The HTTP URI <strong>must</strong> end with <code>:batchDelete</code>.</li>
<li>The URI path <strong>should</strong> represent the collection for the resource, matching
  the collection used for simple CRUD operations. If the operation spans
  parents, a dash (<code>-</code>) <strong>may</strong> be accepted as a wildcard.</li>
<li>The body clause in the <code>google.api.http</code> annotation <strong>should</strong> be <code>"*"</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="atomic-vs-partial-success">Atomic vs. Partial Success</h3>
<ul>
<li>The batch delete method <strong>may</strong> support atomic (all resources deleted or none
  are) or partial success behavior. To make a choice, consider the following
  factors:<ul>
<li><strong>Complexity of Ensuring Atomicity:</strong> Operations that are simple
  passthrough database transactions <strong>should</strong> use an atomic operation,
  while operations that manage complex resources <strong>should</strong> use partial
  success operations.</li>
<li><strong>End-User Experience:</strong> Consider the perspective of the API consumer.
  Would atomic behavior be preferable for the given use case, even if it
  means that a large batch could fail due to issues with a single or a few
  entries?</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Synchronous batch delete <strong>must</strong> be atomic.</li>
<li>Asynchronous batch delete <strong>may</strong> support atomic or partial success.<ul>
<li>If supporting partial success, see
  <a href="#operation-metadata-message">Operation metadata message</a> requirements.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message">Request message</h3>
<p>The request for a batch delete method <strong>should</strong> be specified with the
following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchDeleteBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent resource shared by all books being deleted.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this is set, the parent of all of the books specified in `names`</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// must match this field.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The names of the books to delete.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A maximum of 1000 books can be deleted in a batch.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">names</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included, unless the resource being deleted is
  a top-level resource. If a caller sets this field, and the
  parent collection in the name of any resource being deleted does not match,
  the request <strong>must</strong> fail.<ul>
<li>This field <strong>should</strong> be required if only 1 parent per request is allowed.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/122#fields-representing-a-resources-parent">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> include a repeated field which accepts the
  resource names specifying the resources to delete. The field <strong>should</strong> be
  named <code>names</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be required.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/122#fields-representing-resource-names">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Other fields besides <code>name</code> <strong>may</strong> be "hoisted" from the <a href="/135#request-message">standard Delete
  request</a>. There is no way to allow for these fields to
  accept different values for different resources; if this is needed, use the
  <a href="#request-message-containing-standard-delete-request-messages">alternative request message form</a>.</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
<li>The comment above the <code>names</code> field <strong>should</strong> document the maximum number of
  requests allowed.</li>
<li>Filter-based matching <strong>must not</strong> be supported.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="request-message-containing-standard-delete-request-messages">Request message containing standard delete request messages</h3>
<p>If the <a href="/135#request-message">standard Delete request message</a> contains a field
besides the resource name that needs to be different between different
resources being requested, the batch message <strong>may</strong> alternatively hold a
<code>repeated</code> field of the <a href="/135#request-message">standard Delete request message</a>.
This is generally discouraged unless your use case really requires it.</p>
<p>The request for a batch delete method <strong>should</strong> be specified with the
following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchDeleteBooksRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The parent resource shared by all books being deleted.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Format: publishers/{publisher}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// If this is set, the parent of all of the books specified in the</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// DeleteBookRequest messages must match this field.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="kt">string</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">parent</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">google.api.resource_reference</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="n">child_type</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;library.googleapis.com/Book&quot;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}];</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// The requests specifying the books to delete.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// A maximum of 1000 books can be deleted in a batch.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">DeleteBookRequest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">requests</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">[(</span><span class="n">google.api.field_behavior</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">REQUIRED</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>A <code>parent</code> field <strong>should</strong> be included. If a caller sets this field, and the
  parent collection in the name of any resource being deleted does not match,
  the request <strong>must</strong> fail.<ul>
<li>This field <strong>should</strong> be required if only 1 parent per request is allowed.</li>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> identify the <a href="/122#fields-representing-a-resources-parent">resource type</a> that it
  references.</li>
<li>The comment for the field <strong>should</strong> document the resource pattern.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> include a repeated field which accepts the
  request messages specifying the resources to delete, as specified for
  <a href="/135#request-message">standard Delete methods</a>. The field <strong>should</strong> be named
  <code>requests</code>.<ul>
<li>The field <strong>should</strong> be required.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Other fields <strong>may</strong> be "hoisted" from the <a href="/135#request-message">standard Delete
  request</a>, which means that the field can be set at either
  the batch level or child request level. Similar to <code>parent</code>, if both the
  batch level and child request level are set for the same field, the values
  <strong>must</strong> match.<ul>
<li>Fields which must be unique cannot be hoisted (e.g. <code>etag</code>).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The request message <strong>must not</strong> contain any other required fields, and
  <strong>should not</strong> contain other optional fields except those described in this
  or another AIP.</li>
<li>The comment above the <code>requests</code> field <strong>should</strong> document the maximum number
  of requests allowed.</li>
<li>Filter-based matching <strong>must not</strong> be supported unless it is infeasible to
  support critical use cases without it, because it makes it too easy for users
  to accidentally delete important data. If it is unavoidable, see <a href="/165">AIP-165</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="response-message-soft-delete-only">Response message (soft-delete only)</h3>
<p>In the case where a response message is necessary because the resource is
soft-deleted, the response <strong>should</strong> be specified with the following pattern:</p>
<div class="highlight language-proto"><pre><span></span><code><span class="kd">message</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nc">BatchDeleteBooksResponse</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Books deleted.</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">repeated</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Book</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">books</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<ul>
<li>The response message <strong>must</strong> include one repeated field corresponding to the
  resources that were soft-deleted.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="operation-metadata-message">Operation metadata message</h3>
<ul>
<li>The <code>metadata_type</code> message <strong>must</strong> either match the RPC name with
  <code>OperationMetadata</code> suffix, or be named with <code>Batch</code> prefix and
  <code>OperationMetadata</code> suffix if the type is shared by multiple Batch methods.</li>
<li>If batch delete method supports partial success, the metadata message <strong>must</strong>
  include a <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field to communicate
  the partial failures.<ul>
<li>The key in this map is the index of the request in the <code>requests</code> field in
  the batch request.</li>
<li>The value in each map entry <strong>must</strong> mirror the error(s) that would normally
  be returned by the singular Standard Delete method.</li>
<li>If a failed request can eventually succeed due to server side retries, such
  transient errors <strong>must not</strong> be communicated using <code>failed_requests</code>.</li>
<li>When all requests in the batch fail, <code>Operation.error</code> <strong>must</strong> be set with
  <code>code = google.rpc.Code.Aborted</code> and <code>message = "None of the requests
  succeeded, refer to the BatchDeleteBooksOperationMetadata.failed_requests
  for individual error details"</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The metadata message <strong>may</strong> include other fields to communicate the
  operation progress.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="adopting-partial-success">Adopting Partial Success</h3>
<p>In order for an existing Batch API to adopt the partial success pattern, the API
must do the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>The default behavior must be retained to avoid incompatible behavioral
  changes.</li>
<li>If the API returns an Operation:<ul>
<li>The request message <strong>must</strong> have a <code>bool return_partial_success</code> field.</li>
<li>The Operation <code>metadata_type</code> <strong>must</strong> include a
  <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field.</li>
<li>When the <code>bool return_partial_success</code> field is set to true in a request,
  the API should allow partial success behavior, otherwise it should continue
  with atomic behavior as default.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If the API returns a direct response synchronously:<ul>
<li>Since the existing clients will treat a success response as an atomic
  operation, the existing version of the API <strong>must not</strong> adopt the partial
  success pattern.</li>
<li>A new version <strong>must</strong> be created instead that returns an Operation and
  follows the partial success pattern described in this AIP.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="rationale">Rationale</h2>
<h3 id="restricting-synchronous-batch-methods-to-be-atomic">Restricting synchronous batch methods to be atomic</h3>
<p>The restriction that synchronous batch methods must be atomic is a result of
the following considerations.</p>
<p>The previous iteration of this AIP recommended batch methods must be atomic.
There is no clear way to convey partial failure in a sync response status code
because an OK implies it all worked. Therefore, adding a new field to the
response to indicate partial failure would be a breaking change because the
existing clients would interpret an OK response as all resources created.</p>
<p>On the other hand, as described in <a href="https://aip.dev/193">AIP-193</a>, Operations
are more capable of presenting partial states. The response status code for an
Operation does not convey anything about the outcome of the underlying operation
and a client has to check the response body to determine if the operation was
successful.</p>
<h3 id="communicating-partial-failures">Communicating partial failures</h3>
<p>The AIP recommends using a <code>map&lt;int32, google.rpc.Status&gt; failed_requests</code> field
to communicate partial failures, where the key is the index of the failed
request in the original batch request. The other options considered were:</p>
<ul>
<li>A <code>repeated google.rpc.Status</code> field. This was rejected because it is not
  clear which entry corresponds to which request.</li>
<li>A <code>map&lt;string, google.rpc.Status&gt;</code> field, where the key is the request id of
  the failed request. This was rejected because:<ul>
<li>Client will need to maintain a map of request_id -&gt; request in order to use
  the partial success response.</li>
<li>Populating a request id for the purpose of communicating errors could
  conflict with <a href="https://aip.dev/155">AIP-155</a> if the service can not
  guarantee idempotency for an individual request across multiple batch
  requests.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>A <code>repeated FailedRequest</code> field, where FailedRequest contains the individual
  create request and the <code>google.rpc.Status</code>. This was rejected because echoing
  the request payload back in response is discouraged due to additional
  challenges around user data sensitivity.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="changelog">Changelog</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2025-03-06</strong>: Changed recommendation to allow partial success, along with
  detailed guidance</li>
<li><strong>2022-06-02:</strong> Changed suffix descriptions to eliminate superfluous "-".</li>
<li><strong>2020-09-16</strong>: Suggested annotating <code>parent</code>, <code>names</code>, and <code>requests</code> fields.</li>
<li><strong>2020-08-27</strong>: Removed parent recommendations for top-level resources.</li>
<li><strong>2020-03-27</strong>: Added reference to <a href="/165">AIP-165</a> for criteria-based deletion.</li>
<li><strong>2019-10-11</strong>: Changed the primary recommendation to specify a repeated
  string instead of a repeated standard Delete message. Moved the original
  recommendation into its own section.</li>
<li><strong>2019-09-11</strong>: Fixed the wording about which child field the <code>parent</code> field
  should match.</li>
<li><strong>2019-08-01</strong>: Changed the examples from "shelves" to "publishers", to
  present a better example of resource ownership.</li>
</ul>
